articles.title: Casarão de 150 anos vira museu e preserva história em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Imóvel pertenceu ao coronel Carlos José Bernardes Sobrinho, fundador de Lagoa da Prata. Museu homenageia a esposa dele, Alexandrina Henriquina de São José, que assumiu os negócios da família após a morte do marido. Programação cultural gratuita segue até domingo (22).
articles.summary: O Museu Dona Alexandrina preserva a história de Lagoa da Prata em um casarão de 150 anos restaurado, oferecendo programação cultural gratuita até este domingo.
articles.body:
Um casarão histórico de cerca de 150 anos, que pertenceu ao fundador de Lagoa da Prata , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, foi reaberto nesta semana como museu. O imóvel, construído em 1875, passou por uma reforma de R$ 2 milhões e agora leva o nome de Museu Dona Alexandrina , em homenagem à esposa do coronel Carlos José Bernardes Sobrinho , fundador da cidade.

Tombado pelo município, o casarão já teve diferentes proprietários e abrigou a Câmara Municipal e a Biblioteca Municipal. Em 2023, o imóvel voltou a pertencer à Prefeitura e passou por uma reforma para recuperar a estrutura, que estava bastante deteriorada.

Para celebrar a reabertura, a Prefeitura preparou uma programação cultural gratuita, com shows, oficinas, palestras e apresentações artísticas, que segue até domingo (22). As atividades acontecem no próprio museu. Confira a programação completa ao final da reportagem .

Conhecido inicialmente como Solar dos Bernardes, o casarão foi construído em 1875, próximo à lagoa, por iniciativa do coronel Carlos José Bernardes Sobrinho. Feito de adobe e pau a pique, em estilo colonial português, o imóvel tinha 19 cômodos ricamente decorados.

Ao longo dos anos, o casarão passou por diferentes proprietários e teve diversas funções. Em 2023, voltou a ser propriedade do município, dando início ao processo de recuperação para abrigar o museu.

Segundo a secretária municipal de Cultura, Laiana Modesto, foram investidos R$ 2 milhões em recursos próprios da Prefeitura na reconstrução do imóvel, que estava bastante deteriorado.

Embora tenha sido reaberto, o museu ainda passa pelos preparativos para receber o público. De acordo com a secretária, o plano museológico e os detalhes do acervo já estão definidos.

A proposta é transformar o casarão em um espaço dedicado à preservação da memória de Lagoa da Prata. Para isso, alguns ambientes serão recriados como eram na época da construção, enquanto o acervo reunirá documentos e outros materiais que ajudam a contar a história da cidade. O museu também deverá receber exposições culturais.

Descendentes do fundador ainda vivem em Lagoa da Prata

A história do casarão também faz parte da memória de famílias que continuam vivendo em Lagoa da Prata. Uma delas é a de Rosana Bahia Lobato, bisneta do coronel Carlos José Bernardes Sobrinho e de Alexandrina Henriquina de São José.

Rosana voltou a morar na cidade há cerca de dez anos e acompanha com entusiasmo a recuperação do imóvel que pertenceu aos bisavós. Para ela, a reabertura representa não apenas a preservação da história da família, mas também um avanço para o patrimônio cultural do município.

“É um grande passo para Lagoa da Prata, ver o museu sendo reaberto, resgatado, grande passo para a memória, para o patrimônio. O museu é uma grande referência para a cidade. É muito bom que por estar próximo da prainha, quem vier pode vir conhecer o museu”, afirmou.

Socióloga, Rosana conta que sempre teve interesse em conhecer o passado da família e que as conversas com a avó ajudaram a manter vivas essas lembranças.

“A família é grande, sempre fui interessada, conversava muito com a minha avó”, contou.

Registro histórico de Alexandrina Henriquina de São José e do marido, coronel Carlos José Bernardes Sobrinho, fundador de Lagoa da Prata (MG) — Foto: Rosana Bahia Lobato/Arquivo Pessoal

O nome escolhido para o museu homenageia Alexandrina Henriquina de São José, prima e esposa do coronel Carlos José Bernardes Sobrinho.

Após a morte do marido, em 1900, foi Alexandrina quem assumiu a administração dos diversos negócios da família, permanecendo à frente deles até morrer, em 1930.

Para a bisneta Rosana Bahia Lobato, a trajetória de Alexandrina faz dela uma figura importante na história de Lagoa da Prata. Ela considera que a bisavó pode ser lembrada como uma das primeiras empresárias da cidade, em uma época em que a participação feminina à frente dos negócios não era comum.

Agora, o nome de Alexandrina passa a identificar o espaço dedicado à preservação da memória e da história do município.

Para celebrar a reabertura do Museu Dona Alexandrina, a Prefeitura de Lagoa da Prata preparou três dias de atividades culturais gratuitas, com apresentações musicais, oficinas, rodas de conversa e atrações que valorizam a história e as tradições da cidade.

A programação acontece de sexta-feira (20) a domingo (22), no Museu Dona Alexandrina, localizado na Praça Dona Alexandrina, nº 145, no Bairro Santa Alexandrina. Confira:

14h: Oficina de Boneca Abayomi, com a Secretaria Municipal de Cultura e Turismo (Sectur).

15h: Sarau "Vozes Negras Importam", com participação da Acadelp, Clube do Livro e Academia Jovem.

16h: Roda de capoeira com o Grupo Afro-Minas.

17h: Apresentação da Associação Cultural e Tradicional de Matriz Africana Bakise Kukuet Mukongo Kiamaza.

17h30: Roda de conversa sobre a importância do povo negro na construção de Lagoa da Prata.

20h: Apresentação do Coral Congo Rosário de Maria.

15h30: Abertura oficial, palestra, entrega de medalhas e lançamento do livro "Prosa e Verso".

19h: Apresentação do grupo musical Acadelp em Seresta.

11h30: Apresentação do Coral Vozes de Prata.

12h: Show com Aron, violeiro da Canastra.

VÍDEOS: veja tudo sobre o Centro-Oeste de Minas

articles.title: Desocupação no Amapá cai pelo 2º trimestre seguido, aponta IBGE | G1
articles.standfirst: Esse é o 2º trimestre consecutivo em que o estado apresenta queda na taxa de desocupados.
articles.summary: A desocupação no Amapá recuou para 7,9% com a criação de 3,4 mil novos postos de trabalho, mantendo a tendência de queda pelo segundo trimestre consecutivo em 2026.
articles.body:
Amapá tem queda na taxa de desocupação no 3º trimestre. — Foto: Ascom

O Amapá registrou queda de 1,9 ponto percentual na taxa de desocupação no 3º trimestre de 2026, segundo dados da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (PNAD) Contínua, divulgada pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

Esse é o 2º trimestre consecutivo em que o estado apresenta queda na taxa de desocupados. No trimestre anterior, a taxa foi de 9,8%, 0,2 ponto percentual menor que a do 1º trimestre do ano, que foi de 10%.

Dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged) mostram que, entre junho e setembro, surgiram mais de 3,4 mil novas vagas de emprego, com destaque para o setor de serviços, que concentra 61% dessas oportunidades.

Além do Amapá, outros sete estados apresentaram queda na taxa de desocupação: Bahia (-2,0%), Piauí (-1,5%), Alagoas (-1,2%), Rio Grande do Norte (-1,1%), Distrito Federal (-1,0%), Ceará (-0,9%) e Paraíba (-0,9%). O estado do Espírito Santo apresentou alta (+0,7%), enquanto as demais 18 unidades da Federação mantiveram estabilidade estatística.

Apesar da redução, o estado ainda possui a segunda maior taxa de desocupados do país, com 7,9%, atrás apenas de Pernambuco (8,6%). O índice está acima da média nacional (5,2%) e da Região Norte (5,6%). O rendimento médio real habitual do Amapá foi estimado em R$ 3.139, ficando abaixo da média nacional, avaliada em R$ 3.790.

articles.title: VÍDEO: motorista erra manobra, invade loja de tintas com carro e causa prejuízo estimado em R$ 100 mil no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu em Marechal Cândido Rondon. Câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que o veículo atingiu a fachada do estabelecimento. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu em Marechal Cândido Rondon. Câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que o veículo atingiu a fachada do estabelecimento. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.body:
Uma motorista invadiu uma loja de tintas com o carro após uma manobra no estacionamento do estabelecimento, em Marechal Cândido Rondon , no oeste do Paraná, na manhã desta sexta-feira (20). Câmeras de segurança registraram o acidente, que causou um prejuízo estimado em R$ 100 mil, segundo o proprietário. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Nas imagens, é possível ver o momento em que a motorista, que estava em um carro vermelho, começa a sair do estacionamento. Ela dá ré, mas, em seguida, o veículo avança para a frente e atinge a fachada da loja. Veja o vídeo acima.

Uma pedestre aparece passando pela calçada momentos antes de o carro atingir o estabelecimento.

Com o impacto, parte da fachada foi destruída e vários galões de tinta foram danificados.

Carro invadiu loja de tintas — Foto: RPC Cascavel

O proprietário estima que os prejuízos cheguem a R$ 100 mil, considerando os danos à estrutura e a perda de mercadorias.

Segundo o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), a motorista é uma idosa e recusou atendimento médico.

Não há informações sobre o que provocou a manobra que terminou no acidente.

articles.title: Meteoro na Paraíba: Câmera registra clarão intenso no céu | G1
articles.standfirst: Clarão surpreendeu paraibanos. O fenômeno também foi observado em estados vizinhos.
articles.summary: Meteoro na Paraíba: fenômeno inesperado causou um clarão intenso visto em diversos estados do Nordeste e foi registrado por câmeras de monitoramento em João Pessoa.
articles.body:
A passagem de um meteoro chamou a atenção de moradores de João Pessoa e outras cidades da Paraíba na noite da quinta-feira (19). O fenômeno foi registrado por uma câmera de monitoramento e também por pessoas que testemunharam o clarão no céu.

O registro, divulgado pelo astrofotógrafo Marcelo Zurita, foi feito às 21h34 a partir de João Pessoa. Ele mostra o momento exato em que o meteoro passou pela Paraíba.

As imagens mostram um clarão intenso cruzando o céu, o rastro luminoso dura poucos segundos antes de desaparecer.

Passagem de meteoro é registrada na Paraíba — Foto: Divulgação/Marcelo Zurita

De acordo com Marcelo Zurita, o meteoro foi visto em todo o estado da Paraíba e também em estados vizinhos, como Rio Grande do Norte, Pernambuco, Ceará e Alagoas.

Ainda segundo ele, o fenômeno não era esperado.

"Estamos no período da chuva de meteoros Leônidas, mas esse meteoro não fazia parte dela", explicou.

A Associação Paraibana de Astronomia (APA) estima que o meteoro tenha deixado fragmentos, chamados meteoritos, na região de Pocinhos e Nazaré. Marcelo Zurita orienta a população a entrar em contato com a APA, caso encontrem rochas com uma crosta escura, diferente das outras da região, para que sejam avaliadas.

Um meteoro é um fenômeno luminoso gerado pela passagem de uma rocha espacial pela atmosfera em alta velocidade. A velocidade é tão grande que a rocha comprime os gases atmosféricos à sua frente, provocando o clarão de luz.

Zurita explica que ao passar pela atmosfera, normalmente, todos os fragmentos de rocha espacial são vaporizados completamente. Quando a rocha é maior, ela pode resistir e chegar ao solo na forma de meteorito.

articles.title: Secretária de Trump é proibida de enviar e-mails religiosos | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão afirma que mensagens davam a entender que funcionários compartilhavam das crenças cristãs da secretária.
articles.summary: A secretária de Trump, Brooke Rollins, foi proibida de enviar e-mails religiosos por canais oficiais após a Justiça apontar pressão sobre funcionários federais.
articles.body:
Secretária de Agricultura dos EUA, Brooke Rollins, durante evento em Kerrville, no Texas. — Foto: Kaylee Greenlee/Reuters

Uma juíza dos Estados Unidos determinou que a secretária de Agricultura, Brooke Rollins, pare de enviar e-mails de conteúdo religioso a funcionários por meio de sua conta oficial, afirmando que Rollins "deve reconhecer" limites ao transmitir mensagens religiosas e que algumas das palavras usadas por ela pressupunham que os destinatários dos e-mails compartilhavam de suas crenças cristãs.

"O Tribunal DETERMINA que a secretária deve reconhecer certos limites ao transmitir mensagens religiosas", afirmou a juíza distrital dos EUA Trina Thompson na decisão desta quinta-feira (19).

Rollins, uma cristã devota, enviou com frequência mensagens religiosas celebrando sua fé cristã por meio de seu e-mail oficial e de suas contas nas redes sociais, o que levou grupos de defesa da liberdade religiosa e funcionários federais a entrarem com uma ação judicial sobre o caso.

Defensores da separação entre Igreja e Estado afirmam que altos funcionários do governo do presidente Donald Trump têm adotado práticas que confundem os limites entre governo e religião e não refletem a diversidade do país.

O chefe do Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, incorporou as manifestações sobre sua fé cristã à rotina diária no Pentágono, enquanto especialistas em religião e política afirmam que Trump tem usado retórica cristã para mobilizar seus principais apoiadores em torno da impopular guerra entre EUA e Israel contra o Irã.

O Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. A pasta argumentou que os e-mails de Rollins não eram coercitivos porque ela transmitia suas opiniões pessoais sobre a celebração de determinados feriados, em vez de participar de qualquer prática religiosa ou tentar impor conformidade.

"Este Tribunal não expressa qualquer opinião sobre o que a secretária pode ou não fazer em sua vida pessoal", escreveu a juíza na decisão desta quinta-feira.

Os autores da ação alegaram que as mensagens de Rollins transmitiam uma preferência por funcionários que compartilhavam suas crenças cristãs, ao mesmo tempo em que faziam com que os demais se sentissem excluídos e pressionados a esconder suas próprias crenças ou a aparentar compartilhar das dela.

A ação alegou que supervisores haviam alertado que objeções resultariam em "problemas".

"O uso pela secretária de 'nós', 'nos' e 'nosso' [na comunicação], juntamente com sua incapacidade de reconhecer outros feriados religiosos ou admitir que outros funcionários possam ter crenças diferentes, expressa uma cultura e um ambiente dentro do Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA que, aparentemente, se conformam universalmente às crenças da secretária", escreveu a juíza.

Defensores dos direitos civis também afirmam que a retórica eleitoral de Trump e de seus aliados contra grupos como americanos muçulmanos e somalis, assim como uma repressão mais ampla à imigração e às iniciativas de diversidade, causou preocupação entre minorias étnicas.

Cerca de 62% dos adultos nos Estados Unidos se identificam como cristãos, segundo o Religious Landscape Study.

articles.title: FOTOS mostram como seca transformou principal rio de Roraima | G1
articles.standfirst: O nível do rio baixou mais de 30 centímetros em um mês em Boa Vista. Imagens mostram bancos de areia e extensas áreas com terra exposta.
articles.summary: O nível do rio baixou mais de 30 centímetros em um mês em Boa Vista. Imagens mostram bancos de areia e extensas áreas com terra exposta.
articles.body:
Trechos do Rio Branco, em Boa Vista , viraram um "tapete de areia" em meio à seca que atinge o estado. Com a redução do nível da água, extensos bancos de areia ficaram expostos e mudaram a paisagem do rio , o principal de Roraima .

O nível do rio baixou mais de 30 centímetros em um mês na capital e chegou a 15 centímetros nesta quinta-feira (19) , conforme a régua que mede o nível do rio. No trecho que passa por Caracaraí , no Sul de Roraima, o nível da água caiu de 93 centímetros em 19 de outubro para 59 nesta quinta .

O cenário é diferente de cinco meses atrás, quando o rio chegou a mais de 9 metros e entrou em cota de inundação em Caracaraí , e de alerta na capital . Na época, em Boa Vista, a água do rio Branco chegou a se aproximar das escadarias do Parque do Rio Branco, um dos principais pontos turísticos.

O g1 separou imagens que mostram o antes e o depois da seca no rio. Confira abaixo.

Veja o antes e o depois do Rio Branco em Boa Vista:

Vista aérea da Ponte dos Macuxis, sobre o rio Branco, durante chuvas em maio de 2026. — Foto: Jonathas Oliveira/PMBV/Reprodução

Mirante Edileusa Lóz, um dos principais pontos turísticos de Boa Vista (RR) — Foto: Reprodução/Will Manaiuama/PMBV

Vista aérea do Rio Branco, em Boa Vista (RR), em agosto de 2026. — Foto: Bruno Rayleno/PMBV/Reprodução

Rio Branco em setembro de 2026. — Foto: Ronny Alcântara/Rede Amazônica

Pilares da Ponte do Macuxi, sobre o rio Branco, em 8 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Will Manuiama/PMBV/Reprodução

Rio Branco, em Boa Vista (RR), em novembro de 2026. — Foto: Raquel Maia/Rede Amazônica/Amazônia Agro

Trecho do rio Branco em Boa Vista (RR), em novembro de 2026. — Foto: Will Manuiama/PMBV/Reprodução

Ponte dos Macuxis sobre o rio Branco, em Boa Vista (RR), em novembro de 2026. — Foto: Raquel Maia/Amazônia Agro/Rede Amazônica

A queda no nível do rio ocorre durante o período de seca em Roraima, que tradicionalmente vai de outubro a março. Boa parte do território está no Hemisfério Norte e, por isso, o estado passa pelo chamado "verão amazônico" , época em que as chuvas diminuem e o calor se intensifica .

Desde setembro, Roraima está em situação de emergência devido à estiagem. A medida, que vale até março, foi adotada de forma preventiva diante das previsões de uma estiagem de forte intensidade.

Ela autoriza a mobilização dos órgãos estaduais para ações de monitoramento, prevenção, assistência humanitária e recuperação das áreas afetadas.

Dados da plataforma Alerta Secas, do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden), apontam que 11 dos 15 municípios do estado estão em situação de alerta para secas em novembro. Pacaraima, São Luiz, São João da Baliza e Caroebe são os únicos em atenção.

Em 10 de novembro, a Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA) decretou, pela primeira vez, situação crítica de escassez nos rios Maú e Tacutu , afluentes do rio Branco . A medida é válida até abril de 2027, quando termina o período seco e começa o chuvoso no estado.

articles.title: Pix de R$ 5 mil para MEIs não terá valor reduzido para R$ 363 | G1
articles.standfirst: Posts mentem ao dizer que os R$ 5 bilhões do benefício serão divididos entre os 13,78 milhões de MEIs ativos no Brasil. Ao Fato ou Fake, Secretaria de Comunicação da Presidência desmente conteúdo e diz: 'Política prevê atendimento de cerca de 1 milhão de microempreendedores'.
articles.summary: Posts mentem ao dizer que os R$ 5 bilhões do benefício serão divididos entre os 13,78 milhões de MEIs ativos no Brasil. Ao Fato ou Fake, Secretaria de Comunicação da Presidência desmente conteúdo e diz: 'Política prevê atendimento de cerca de 1 milhão de microempreendedores'.
articles.body:
Não é verdde que assistência a MEIs será reduzida de R$ 5 mil para R$ 363 — Foto: g1

Circulam nas redes sociais publicações sugerindo que o Pix MEI, proposta de incentivo financeiro de até R$ 5 mil a microempreendedores individuais anunciada por Lula ( PT ) durante a campanha à reeleição, terá de baixar para R$ 363 caber no "orçamento" reservado pelo governo. É #FAKE.

Publicações que viralizaram a partir de 2 de novembro no Facebook, no X e no TikTok exibem uma foto do presidente acompanhada da seguinte mensagem: "Pix de R$ 5.000 prometido por Lula na campanha para agradar Microempreendedores Individuais (MEIs) pode acabar sendo de apenas R$ 363".

Veja um exemplo de legenda: "O Pix de R$ 5 mil prometido por Lula aos MEIs durante sua campanha para a reeleição pode ter um valor muito menor. Com mais de 17 milhões de MEls registrados e mais de 13 milhões ativos, o governo precisaria de quase R$ 70 bilhões para cumprir a promessa do petista. Entretanto, o governo fala em reservar R$ 5 bilhões, que, se [forem] distribuídos a cada MEI, o valor real seria de apenas R$ 363".

Mas a lei aprovada pelo Congresso e sancionada por Lula não prevê repasses a todos os 13,8 milhões de números ativos no Cadastro Nacional da Pessoa Jurídica (CNPJs) que se enquadram na categoria MEI. Na verdade, trata-se de 7,5% dessa cifra, como informou ao Fato ou Fake a Secretaria de Comunicação Social da Presidência (Secom), em nota enviada por e-mail.

Leia a resposta: "A política pública prevê o atendimento de cerca de 1 milhão de microempreendedores a partir de 2027, somando R$ 5 bilhões em investimentos produtivos, com acompanhamento do Sebrae [Serviço Brasileiro de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas]. A seleção dará prioridade no atendimento a mulheres empreendedoras — que já respondem por 48% dos registros de MEI no país — e a MEIs com faturamento de até R$ 40,5 mil". Leia mais detalhes abaixo.

O Pix MEI integra o Prospera MEI, um pacote de assistência ao microempreendedor anunciado pelo governo em 14 de outubro , entre o primeiro e o segundo turno das eleições 2026 , que terminou com a vitória de Lula (PT) sobre Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ).

A iniciativa prevê, entre outros pontos, o aumento do teto de faturamento anual de R$ 81 mil para R$ 110 mil em 2027 e R$ 140 mil em 2028; o perdão de dívidas tributárias federais; e a contratação de até dois funcionários por MEI.

Ao Fato ou Fake , a Secom detalhou: "O dinheiro deve ser aplicado obrigatoriamente na aquisição de bens que gerem desenvolvimento produtivo. Maquinários, ferramentas profissionais, bancadas de trabalho e a reforma e adaptação de veículos utilitários e de entrega são alguns exemplos de projetos que serão aprovados. [...] A transferência direta de até R$ 5 mil por beneficiário ocorrerá na modalidade de capital semente a fundo perdido. Diferentemente de empréstimos bancários, os recursos não precisarão ser devolvidos e não haverá cobrança de juros".

A resposta cita ainda que o Pix MEI está em fase de estruturação e que detalhes da operação, como a forma de inscrição no programa, serão divulgados até o final deste ano.

O site oficial do Ministério das Mulheres divulgou, em 21 de outubro, uma nota intitulada "Do alívio nas dívidas ao investimento no negócio, conheça as medidas do Prospera MEI para mulheres".

O comunicado menciona que a previsão inicial não era a de que a medida incluiria automaticamente todos os MEIs do país: "O incentivo não será pago automaticamente a todas as pessoas registradas como MEI. Será necessário observar os critérios, os prazos e os procedimentos de seleção que forem publicados" .

articles.title: Homem morre ao ser atropelado por caminhonete na SP-75 em Salto | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima morreu no local e o motorista saiu ileso. Todas as faixas e o acostamento ficaram interditados por quase quatro horas, mas já foram liberadas.
articles.summary: Um homem morreu ao ser atropelado por uma caminhonete na Rodovia Santos Dumont (SP-75), em Salto  (SP), na noite de quinta-feira (19).
articles.body:
Homem morreu ao ser atropelado por uma caminhonete na Rodovia Santos Dumont (SP-75), em Salto (SP) — Foto: Portal CCM – Artesp/Divulgação

Um homem morreu ao ser atropelado por uma caminhonete na Rodovia Santos Dumont (SP-75), em Salto (SP), na noite de quinta-feira (19).

De acordo com a concessionária que administra o trecho, o acidente aconteceu na altura do quilômetro 42, quando o motorista foi surpreendido pelo pedestre na faixa de rolamento.

Sem tempo para frear, o motorista acabou atropelando a vítima, que morreu no local. O motorista da caminhonete não se feriu.

Houve interdição de todas as faixas e do acostamento por quase quatro horas para atendimento da ocorrência, mas a via já foi liberada.

articles.title: Casal de pescadores faz sucesso nas reeds com pescarias no rio Uruguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Juninho, de Terra Roxa (SP), e a esposa, Rosa, pescam piaparas no rio Uruguai, no Rio Grande do Sul, e compartilham o hobby e o companheirismo.
articles.summary: Juninho, de Terra Roxa (SP), e a esposa, Rosa, pescam piaparas no rio Uruguai, no Rio Grande do Sul, e compartilham o hobby e o companheirismo.
articles.body:
Um casal de pescadores do interior de São Paulo faz sucesso nas redes sociais com vídeos de pescarias no rio Uruguai , no Rio Grande do Sul. Juninho, de 50 anos, divide a paixão pela pesca esportiva com a esposa, Rosa, e acumula milhares de seguidores na internet.

Neste sábado (21), a equipe do Terra da Gente acompanha as aventuras da dupla.

Casal de pescadores faz sucesso na internet com pescarias no rio Uruguai — Foto: Reprodução / Terra da Gente

Unidos pelo amor e pela pesca, casal faz sucesso nas redes sociais — Foto: Reprodução / Terra da Gente

Por trás das imagens de aventura que Juninho compartilha, existe uma parceria que vai além da pesca. Uma história de amor, companheirismo e paixão pela natureza .

Rosa foi quem incentivou o marido a pescar. Quando criança, ela costumava pescar com o avô e, por meio do passatempo, conquistou Juninho e o levou para as águas.

Os vídeos das aventuras da dupla repercutiram na internet, e o perfil de Juninho nas redes sociais já acumula mais de 65 mil seguidores.

Ela o ensinou a pescar; hoje, casal faz sucesso na internet com aventuras no rio Uruguai — Foto: Reprodução / Terra da Gente

O rio Uruguai, onde começou a história de Juninho com a pesca e as redes sociais, fica a quase 1.500 quilômetros de Terra Roxa (SP), cidade do pescador, próxima de Ribeirão Preto e Barretos.

Em busca de piaparas grandes, Juninho fisgou um exemplar de mais de 8 kg e 85 centímetros, que chegou a virar capa de revista.

Casal compartilha paixão pela pesca e conquista mais de 65 mil seguidores na internet — Foto: Reprodução / Terra da Gente

A piapara ( Leporinus obtusidens ) é um peixe migratório que se alimenta de grãos, sementes, vegetais, invertebrados e peixes pequenos. A espécie prefere águas profundas.

Um dos bordões de Juninho é: “só pega peixe quem pesca”. Entre linhas, anzóis e muitos peixes, a dupla faz do barco o quintal de casa.

Acompanhe essa história neste sábado, no Terra da Gente, também pelo globoplay .

articles.title: Pessoas pretas recebem quase 40% menos que brancas em Goiás, diz IBGE | G1
articles.standfirst: Enquanto a média da renda principal de pessoas brancas é de R$ 4.497 por mês, as pretas ganham R$ 2.762. Informalidade atinge 42,7% das pessoas pretas no estado.
articles.summary: Enquanto a fonte de renda principal de pessoas brancas é de R$ 4.497 por mês, as pretas ganham, em média, R$ 2.762. Informalidade atinge 42,7% das pessoas pretas no estado.
articles.body:
O rendimento do trabalho de pessoas pretas é quase 40% inferior ao recebido pelas brancas, em Goiás. O dado foi divulgado na publicação Desigualdades Sociais por Cor ou Raça no Brasil, do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

Segundo dados da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (PNAD Contínua), o rendimento médio habitual do trabalho principal da população goiana em 2025 foi de R$ 3.535 por mês.

A renda, no entanto, muda significativamente quando observados os recortes entre pessoas pretas e brancas:

O percentual de 38,6% abaixo do valor recebido pelos brancos é o segundo maior da série histórica da pesquisa, iniciada em 2012. A desigualdade foi maior que a deste ano apenas em 2023, quando o rendimento de pessoas pretas, então de R$ 2.488, chegou a ser 39,2% menor que o das brancas, que recebiam, em média, R$ 4.094.

Em nenhum ano, desde 2012, os trabalhadores pretos de Goiás tiveram renda média do trabalho principal superior à dos brancos.

Em todo o Brasil, a diferença entre as rendas de pretos e pardos é ainda maior: R$ 2.585 contra R$ 4.425, representando um 41,6% menos.

Região da 44 em Goiânia, Goiás — Foto: Wildes Barbosa/O Popular

A pesquisa também mostra que, em Goiás, 42,7% das pessoas pretas ocupadas trabalhavam em ocupações informais em 2025. O percentual é superior ao de trabalhadores brancos informais, que equivalem a uma parcela de 35,7% do total.

Os dados do IBGE evidenciam, ainda, uma trajetória histórica preocupante sobre o índice de informalidade: Em 2022, as taxas por cor ou raça apresentaram resultados quase idênticos. De lá pra cá, no entanto, elas têm se distanciado ano a ano, com quantidades de pessoas pretas nessa situação muito mais elevadas que as de pessoas brancas.

Todos os dados do instituto se refere à renda principal de pessoas com 14 anos ou mais.

Rendimento do trabalho de pessoas pretas é quase 40% inferior ao recebido pelas brancas, em Goiás, segundo o IBGE — Foto: Natalia Filippin/G1

Outra pesquisa, também divulgada na última quarta-feira (18), revela um cenário que se relaciona diretamente com a renda da população. De acordo com o "Panorama da Diversidade Étnico-Racial no Ensino Superior Brasileiro: Avanços na Inclusão e Desafios na Equidade", a participação de pretos e pardos nas matrículas universitárias, em todo o Brasil, cresceu de 33,9% para 45% entre 2010 e 2024.

Há, no entanto, diferenças significativas na participação desses estudantes entre as diversas áreas de formação. Segundo a pesquisa, realizada pelo Instituto Semesp, entidade que representa mantenedoras de ensino superior do Brasil, com o apoio da MK Estatística, cursos que geralmente proporcionam maiores remunerações apresentam participações bem menores de pretos e pardos, como:

Medicina : apenas 29,3% das matrículas com cor/raça declarada são de estudantes pretos ou pardos, enquanto 68,4% são de brancos.

Esse cenário se inverte quando observados os cursos que, em geral, resultam em salários menores no mercado de trabalho. Nesses, há maior participação de pretos e pardos. Entre os exemplos estão Serviço Social (58,7%), Geografia (55,6%), Enfermagem (55,4%) e Pedagogia (51,5%). Os dados são de 2024.

"Esses dados sugerem a persistência de barreiras de acesso relacionadas a fatores socioeconômicos, custo dos cursos e competitividade dos processos seletivos", afirmou o Semesp.

Os reflexos na renda também foram demonstrados no levantamento. Em 2022, enquanto pessoas brancas com ensino superior concluído tinham um salário médio de R$ 6.547, os pardos recebiam R$ 4.559 e os pretos apenas R$ 4.175.

articles.title: Four men guilty of sex crimes against UK woman drugged by husband
articles.summary: Four British men were convicted on Thursday of raping or sexually abusing a woman who was drugged by her then-husband in a case with echoes of that of Gisele Pelicot, the French woman who became a global symbol in the fight against sexual violence.
articles.body: Four British men were convicted on Thursday of raping or sexually abusing a woman who was drugged by her then-husband in a case with echoes of that of Gisele Pelicot, the French woman who became a global symbol in the fight against sexual violence. Joanne Young, like Pelicot, decided to waive her legal right to anonymity after discovering that her husband at the time had repeatedly drugged her and advertised her for sex online to strangers over more than a decade. Philip Young, a 50-year-old former local councillor, pleaded guilty in January to more than 50 charges against his ex-wife, including 11 counts of rape and charges relating to recording the abuse and publishing it online hundreds of times. “This abuse has cost me my life as I knew it,” Joanne Young said outside court. “The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way.” Call to reconsider law on consent Police discovered the abuse only after an account linked to Philip Young posted bestiality images online in 2024 and then seized his devices, containing videos and images of the abuse. Young’s crimes have striking similarities to those of Dominique Pelicot, who admitted drugging his then-wife Gisele and inviting dozens of men to rape her, prompting a 2024 trial that horrified the world and spurred France to revamp its rape law. Britain’s National Crime Agency said this year it had uncovered a “truly international network” of drug-facilitated rape and sexual assault, which it said was organized online and had members across the world. Law enforcement officials from 10 countries, including the US, are now working on a global operation to target drug-facilitated sexual assaults. Joanne Young said her case “raises serious questions about how the law deals with consent,” adding: “I urge the government to look at this as a priority so that women are properly protected in the future.” Fifth man had pleaded guilty The men found guilty following a trial at Winchester Crown Court, in southern England, had responded to adverts posted by Philip Young, who admitted drugging his wife and inviting strangers to have sex with her, watching and filming while it happened. Richard Clive Wilkins, 62, was convicted of rape and assault by penetration, Norman Macksoni, 48, was also convicted of rape, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, was found guilty of sexual assault and assault by penetration, while Mohammed Hassan, 38, was convicted of one count of sexual assault. In defenses echoing those of many of the 50 co-defendants of Dominique Pelicot who were convicted in France, they said they thought Joanne Young consented and that it was a shared fantasy with her then-husband. She had sat in court as prosecutor Sarah Jones said her ex-husband had posted images online, showing his then-wife tied to her bed and blindfolded, as he “sought strangers to come and sleep with his wife – any age, any race.” After the verdicts were announced, Judge Pushpinder Saini said she had shown “amazing bravery.” A fifth man, Dean Hamilton, 47, had previously admitted rape, assault by penetration and sexual assault. All five, along with Philip Young, will be sentenced next month and Saini said they faced a significant custodial sentence. Pelicot not an isolated case The Pelicot trial horrified the world, but it now appears to be far from an isolated case. Specialist Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor James Foster said the case “marks the first time in England that a jury has convicted men of sexually assaulting a woman, who had been drugged in abuse organized by her husband.” In April, law enforcement bodies from 10 countries, coordinated by Europol, the EU’s law ​enforcement agency, set up “Project Medusa” to tackle the issue, led by investigators from Britain and Germany, and including the US, France and Canada. Those involved have since launched 113 investigations linked to that operation, leading to 57 arrests and 158 safeguarded victims, Europol said in June. The Crown Prosecution Service said British police had spoken with investigators who worked on the Pelicot case and that the toxicology expert whose evidence was used in France had also worked on the case involving Joanne Young. “I live with a pain that’s hard to put into words… it is terrifying that this could happen to anyone,” Young said.

The men raped her while she was drugged by her then-husband between 2016 and 2023.

articles.title: Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
articles.summary: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday in a Houthi attack in the latest blow to the kingdom in its war with the Iran-backed Yemeni group.
articles.body: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday in a Houthi attack in the latest blow to the kingdom in its war with the Iran-backed Yemeni group. Saudi Arabia’s civil defense said a Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh’s financial center caused material damage to several floors of the building and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported, state news agency SPA said. The statement did not identify the tower, but an accompanying photograph published by SPA showed the PIF Tower. The Houthis said they had targeted Riyadh’s financial center twice on Thursday, first at dawn and again in the evening. They also said they had attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Khamis Mushait airbase in southern Saudi Arabia and SADAF Petrochemical Company in Jubail in the kingdom’s Eastern Province. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of these attacks. The kingdom’s foreign ministry said it reserved the right to take “all necessary measures” to defend its sovereignty and protect its citizens and national assets following the Houthi attack. The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of the PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade. It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh’s financial district, with state oil company Aramco’s building hit in a November 8 attack. The King Abdullah Financial District was closed to visitors following the attack. Three sources familiar with the matter said the building had been struck by an incoming Houthi missile. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had “dealt with a missile threat” launched towards Riyadh and that debris had fallen. PIF, which stands for the Public Investment Fund, acknowledged receiving a Reuters request for comment. The Houthis issued no immediate statement on the strike. The Houthis have been firing at Saudi airports and oil infrastructure since Yemen’s frozen civil war reignited in July amid the US-Iran war. On the ground in Yemen, the group has seized swathes of territory from the Saudi-backed government, forcing it to stage a major retreat at the weekend. Residents of the Saudi capital were awoken by a loud boom in the early hours of Thursday. Saudi Arabia’s civil defense issued several warnings of potential danger in Riyadh throughout Thursday, including after the attack, before announcing that the threat had passed. The Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that Saudi aircraft had carried out airstrikes on the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital Sanaa early on Thursday, without providing further details. Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the strikes. Saudi sees campaign stretching well into 2027 The conflict has dealt a blow to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s plans to develop and diversify the economy of Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest oil exporter and a US ally. The prince met US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Riyadh on Wednesday, Cooper’s third publicly reported visit to Saudi Arabia since the Yemen conflict resumed. Reuters reported on Wednesday that Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, according to two Western officials briefed by the Saudis on the kingdom’s plans. A third ​source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. The sources said the Saudis, who replaced the commander of their coalition fighting in Yemen this week, want to see their allies make gains on the ground before they enter any negotiations with the Houthis. Meanwhile, the situation in Yemen has appeared to favour the Houthis, who have seized Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast including the strategically vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, and have surrounded the city of Taiz in highlands overlooking the government’s temporary capital Aden. In the wider war, which began in February when the United States and Israel attacked Iran, there has been no sign of a breakthrough in negotiations mediated by Qatar. Meanwhile, there has been an uptick in hostilities in the Gulf in recent days, with Iran firing at US allies Bahrain and Kuwait and US airstrikes hitting Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen’s government to power ​after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year.

articles.title: A black briefcase, a nuclear arsenal: What Putin's Cheget can actually do
articles.summary: A Russian naval officer carrying President Vladimir Putin's nuclear briefcase, known as the Cheget, was spotted in China's Shenzhen during the
articles.body: A Russian naval officer carrying President Vladimir Putin's nuclear briefcase, known as the Cheget, was spotted in China's Shenzhen during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, drawing attention to the system that allows Russia's president to communicate nuclear launch orders to the military.The rare appearance came as Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in the southern Chinese city for trilateral talks on Thursday. The briefcase was identified during a Russian state television broadcast, when reporter Yevgeny Popov pointed towards the black case and told viewers, “this is the nuclear briefcase”.The naval officer accompanying Putin smiled and confirmed that it was indeed the case used by the Russian president to access the country's nuclear command system. “Unbelievable,” Popov said.The Russian device, called the Cheget, is part of the country's nuclear command-and-control system. While it can transmit orders to use nuclear weapons, it cannot launch them independently. The appearance has also renewed attention on the US equivalent, known as the nuclear football, which routinely travels with the American president but has not been spotted in Shenzhen.Whether Xi travels with a similar portable nuclear command device remains unclear.What is a nuclear briefcase?A nuclear briefcase is a specially equipped portable communication device that connects a country's leader to its military command system and allows the transmission of orders relating to the use of nuclear weapons.The US and Russian systems emerged during the Cold War, when both countries faced the possibility of having to make decisions about nuclear strikes at short notice.However, the popular image of a leader pressing a button to launch nuclear weapons is misleading. The briefcase is part of a much larger communication and command network. Military personnel and established procedures are required to authenticate and execute a nuclear order.The devices are designed to ensure that a country's leadership can communicate with its military command structure even when the president is away from the capital.How do the US nuclear football and Russia's Cheget work?The US nuclear briefcase, popularly known as the nuclear football, predates the 1962 Cuban missile crisis. Historians trace its origins to the administration of former US president Dwight Eisenhower. A declassified memorandum indicates that Eisenhower briefed his successor, John F Kennedy, about the device a day before Kennedy took office in January 1961.The US president also carries a card nicknamed the "biscuit", which contains authentication codes used to verify the president's identity when issuing a nuclear order. The vice president has access to a backup football and authentication codes in case they need to assume presidential authority.According to the Congressional Research Service, the US president alone can authorise the use of nuclear weapons, although the president can seek advice from senior military officials.Russia's equivalent, the Cheget, is named after a mountain in the Caucasus and entered Soviet service in 1983. A naval officer traditionally carries the briefcase for the Russian president.The Cheget connects the president to Russia's central military command and can transmit an order to use nuclear weapons, but it cannot launch them on its own. Russia is believed to have three such briefcases, assigned to the president, the defence minister and the chief of the General Staff.The system operates through Russia's Kazbek command-and-control network, which supports a separate communications system known as Kavkaz. Public accounts differ on how many of the briefcases are required to authenticate a presidential order.Under Russia's published nuclear doctrine, the president has the authority to decide whether to use nuclear weapons.Why do leaders travel with nuclear briefcases?Nuclear briefcases are designed to ensure that a country's leadership can communicate with its military command system regardless of its location. A nuclear crisis could emerge while a president is travelling, attending a summit or staying at a hotel.The portable systems allow leaders to communicate orders or authorise a response without having to be physically present at a military command centre.Their role is also linked to nuclear deterrence, which is based on the belief that an adversary may avoid an attack if it knows the other side retains the ability to retaliate.As economist and strategist Thomas Schelling wrote in his 1966 book Arms and Influence: “The power to hurt is bargaining power.”The appearance of Putin's Cheget in Shenzhen also carries a symbolic dimension. Russian media had earlier shown naval officers carrying similar briefcases during Putin's visit to Beijing in 2023.Simon Mabon, a professor of international politics at Lancaster University, told Al Jazeera that the public display of the device was a political statement.“The fact that Kremlin-backed TV channels showed this tells us a lot,” Mabon said. “This is pure political theatre and a symbolic performance of a man that is conscious his country’s standing in the world is not what it once was.”He added: “Compared to the United States or China, Russia does not have the military or economic capacity it once did – this is an attempt to performatively demonstrate that Russia belongs at that grand table.”Do other nuclear-armed countries have similar briefcases?The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute counts nine nuclear-armed states. However, the US and Russian nuclear briefcases are among the few such systems whose details are publicly documented.In the United Kingdom, only the prime minister can authorise the use of nuclear weapons, according to the House of Commons Library. Each incoming prime minister also writes four handwritten "letters of last resort", one for the commander of each nuclear-armed submarine. These letters contain instructions on what to do if a nuclear attack destroys the British government.In France, the authority to authorise nuclear weapons rests with the president. French newspaper Le Monde reported that former president Nicolas Sarkozy handed over the nuclear codes to his successor, Francois Hollande, when he left office in 2012.China maintains a "no first use" nuclear policy, under which Beijing says it would use nuclear weapons only in response to a nuclear attack by another country. Although China operates its own nuclear command-and-control system and its nuclear arsenal has expanded in recent years, it remains unclear whether Xi travels with a dedicated portable device equivalent to the Cheget or the US nuclear football.In India, the government has said that only the Political Council of the Nuclear Command Authority, chaired by the prime minister, can authorise the use of nuclear weapons. Whether the prime minister carries a comparable portable command device has not been publicly established.Pakistan and North Korea also possess nuclear weapons, while Israel is widely believed to have them. However, reliable public information about whether their leaders travel with similar nuclear briefcases is limited.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Contaminated petrol leaves Yemeni drivers struggling to make ends meet
articles.summary: Drivers in Houthi-controlled areas face rising fuel prices and costly repairs as contaminated petrol damages their cars.
articles.body:
Sanaa, Yemen – Yazan, 28, filled up his car at a petrol station in Sanaa and began a trip towards the city of Ibb to the south.

The journey would usually take about two and a half hours, but as he accelerated along the road, Yazan noticed that the car was struggling to pick up speed.

Yazan, who did not want to give his full name, explained that the harder he pressed the accelerator, the more the engine vibrated. The unusual engine noise and vibration forced him to stop several times on the road.

It eventually took Yazan six hours to reach his destination. He believes the problem was caused by contaminated petrol – fuel mixed with oil and impurities – that he bought in Sanaa.

“The petrol left numerous cars, including mine, with many faults,” Yazan told Al Jazeera. “We pay for the expensive petrol that damages our engines.”

Yazan is not alone. Other drivers in Sanaa have reported similar problems with contaminated and increasingly expensive petrol .

The cause of the issue is disputed. In June, the Sanaa-based Yemen Petroleum Company (YPC), run by the Houthis who have controlled northwest Yemen since 2014, said contaminated fuel was the result of inadequately equipped fuel storage facilities in Hodeidah.

Fuel storage tanks in the port city and the nearby Ras Isa oil terminal have been attacked by Israeli and United States air strikes since 2024, in response to Houthi attacks on Israel and shipping in the Red Sea.

The YPC said that the tanks allowed the company to remove impurities before pumping fuel to the market. With the facilities not functioning, the quality of the fuel is impacted.

But many Yemenis dispute that explanation. According to the Sana’a Center for Strategic Studies, restrictions on fuel imports have led the Houthis to partly rely on importing lower-quality Iranian fuel.

Mohammed Ansi, a Yemeni academic, said regular people were being exploited.

“Fuel shipments are being brought in without any accountability, oversight, or conscience – driven solely by the desire for profit and commissions,” he said.

Fuel imports fell sharply from January to May this year. Compared to the same period in 2025, they fell 73 percent through Houthi-controlled ports and 60 percent through ports controlled by the Yemeni government, according to the World Bank.

The drop is partly a result of the impact of the US-Israeli war on Iran on oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as damage to Yemen’s ports from the various attacks it has faced.

With the crisis continuing, its financial toll on families is mounting amid the escalating war in Yemen.

“Paying for expensive petrol and vehicle repair is a fresh war on our livelihoods. It is draining us,” said Yazan.

A few weeks ago, 20 litres (5.3 gallons) of petrol cost 9,500 Yemeni riyals ($18 at rates set by the Houthis) in Sanaa. The price has since risen to 11,400 Yemeni riyals ($21), an increase of 20 percent.

That is not taking into account the additional repair costs necessary if contaminated fuel gets into a vehicle’s engine.

Yemenis are already struggling to make ends meet, a situation that has gotten worse over a decade of war.

An April report by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said that Yemen’s conflict has led to significant macroeconomic vulnerabilities and a marked decrease in income per capita, leaving more than half of the population in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.

Akram Naji, a taxi driver in Sanaa, is among those struggling to get by, and he is now having to figure out how to pay to fix his car.

Naji said he visited a mechanic in Sanaa’s Maeen district after he heard a strange noise coming from his vehicle’s engine.

“The mechanic identified mechanical problems, including a faulty fuel pump, clogged fuel injectors and reduced engine performance.”

Repairing the damage cost him 55,000 Yemeni riyals (about $100), he said.

“For many taxi drivers here like myself, paying this amount of money immediately is a challenge,” Naji said. “I had to not pay my rent in full and decreased my family’s daily expenses to cover the maintenance costs.”

Ali Beidhani, a mechanical engineer in Sanaa, explained what happens when the contaminated petrol enters a vehicle.

“As I observed, when this oily substance or impurities enter the engine along with the petrol, they accumulate in the combustion system,” Beidhani said. “As this substance is exposed to high temperatures, it becomes highly viscous, almost like glue. This leads to damage to engine valves, clogged fuel injectors, and engine vibrations.”

In severe cases, it can even lead to complete engine failure, Beidhani noted.

He said he had seen many drivers struggle to afford repairs.

“The repair cost could force drivers to borrow money or sell possessions like gold, especially if the engine gets damaged or completely fails. Those who rely on their vehicles to eke out a living suffer the most,” said Beidhani.

Wafiq Saleh, an economic researcher and executive director of the Taiz Centre for Yemeni-Gulf Studies, told Al Jazeera that the spread of contaminated fuel heightens the misery of civilians in the war-torn country.

“Bus or taxi driver or delivery riders or farmers struggle every day to make ends meet. With the spread of contaminated petrol, their jobs are disrupted, and they may find themselves incapable of feeding their families,” said Saleh.

He argues that the authorities in Sanaa “bear full responsibility for importing substandard fuel or supplying the market with adulterated petrol, taking advantage of the lack of accountability”.

“The proliferation of adulterated fuel drains citizens’ savings and threatens the livelihoods of thousands of drivers. Breadwinners shift their focus from feeding their children to fixing their vehicle engines,” said Saleh.

Naji is now cautious whenever he approaches a petrol station to fill up his taxi. He checks the colour of the petrol, hoping to spot any signs of contamination.

“A fault in my car is like a wound in my child’s body; I cannot bear to see either go untreated,” he said.

articles.title: Ten years on, is the UK preparing to undo Brexit?
articles.summary: Leaders from the United Kingdom and European Union have concluded a landmark summit as British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pushes for a closer relationship with the bloc a decade after the Brexit vote.
articles.body: Leaders from the United Kingdom and European Union have concluded a landmark summit as British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pushes for a closer relationship with the bloc a decade after the Brexit vote. A new package of agreements to create new opportunities for young people to live, study and travel on the continent, link emissions trading, and remove trade barriers on food products has been agreed, a UK government spokesperson told CNN on Friday. “The deal is done – negotiations have concluded,” the spokesperson said, while adding that “talks will continue on some areas.” Britain’s center-left Labour government inherited Brexit from its predecessors, the Conservative Party, and has long spoken of “resetting” ties with Brussels. But in the four months since he became prime minister, Burnham has staked out a more bullish position on Europe, appearing willing to revisit the politically charged Brexit debate and take on the right-wing parties that fiercely oppose reversing 2016’s referendum result and reestablishing closer ties with Europe. “The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough,” Burnham said in his first major foreign policy speech on Monday, referencing the 2020 deal under which the country left the EU. Last month, he even said he’d like to see Britain rejoin the bloc in his lifetime but ruled that out in this parliament, alongside crossing his party’s “red lines” from their 2024 manifesto of returning to the single market or customs union, or restoring freedom of movement. Nonetheless, he committed to beginning talks with the EU “about options for our long-term relationship” after Friday’s summit without providing further details or timeline. The cost of Brexit Economists broadly agree that leaving the EU stymied the UK’s economic growth potential – with estimates ranging from 2% to as much as 8% of foregone output. So as the government scrabbles for levers to kickstart economic growth, the EU, as Britain’s biggest trading partner and neighbor, has become part of the conversation. Following Labour’s election in 2024 under Burnham’s predecessor Keir Starmer, it promised to “make Brexit work.” Starmer’s strategy was to reboot the UK-EU relationship by negotiating limited deals and aligning some regulations to ease trade frictions. But Starmer’s technocratic, cautious approach – on Europe and other policy areas – led in large part to his party ousting him this summer. The more confident, media-savvy Burnham emerged in his place. Friday’s summit was largely a product of Starmer’s approach, originally scheduled for earlier this year but delayed when his premiership imploded. Nick Thomas-Symonds, a member of parliament who served as Europe minister under Starmer, told CNN the deal was “90% there” when Burnham’s team took over. Issues like aligning tuition fees for EU students studying at UK universities with those of their British counterparts, a final position on UK participation in the EU’s “Made in Europe” initiative – which threatens to squeeze UK businesses out of European supply chains – and the numbers permitted under a youth mobility scheme were still undecided, he said. It’s unclear if Friday’s talks will move the needle in these areas. A limited ‘reset’? Burnham’s rhetoric on Europe has been more forceful, but his actual approach hasn’t changed “an iota” from Starmer’s, said Anand Menon, a professor at King’s College London and director of the think-tank UK in a Changing Europe. “The only difference is how we talk about the future, and Burnham saying we might consider rejoining,” he told CNN ahead of the summit. “The more people talk about rejoining, the more obviously complicated an undertaking it becomes. I don’t know where Burnham goes on this.” Further changes in the UK-EU relationship are unlikely, Menon added, unless the government compromises on its “red lines.” His assessment echoes that of the EU’s former Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier, who warned earlier this month that the UK cannot “cherry pick” certain elements of the single market. For his part, Thomas-Symonds pointed to more cooperation on immigration, stronger military ties and aligning regulations in other sectors as ways to deepen ties with the EU without breaking party promises. “Obviously, these bigger points are ones that we’re looking at in the next manifesto,” he said. Old wounds run deep Burnham’s ambitious rhetoric has shifted the political conversation. Two campaign groups – both with ties to the original “Vote Leave” campaign – either launched or rebranded this week with the express purpose of opposing any attempts to rejoin the EU. Conservative opposition leader Kemi Badenoch, meanwhile, accused Burnham of having “not learnt the lessons of the past,” arguing that “the problems this country faces today have nothing to do with being in or out of the EU.” Brexit architect Nigel Farage, who leads the hard-right Reform UK party, said that Burnham “has no mandate” to negotiate closer ties with Brussels. David Cameron and Boris Johnson, two former Conservative prime ministers whose premierships were defined by Britain’s divorce from the EU, have likewise cautioned Burnham against reopening old wounds. Notwithstanding the Euroskeptic right flank, who are unlikely ever to vote for Labour, the politics of promising to rejoin the EU might actually be favorable for Burnham, noted Morgan Jones, deputy director of Persuasion UK, an organization that researches public opinion. Polling suggests that if “there were an option to rejoin on 2016 terms tomorrow, it would be resoundingly popular,” she told CNN, saying that it also appeals to the different voters Labour would need to win a parliamentary majority. But the same cannot be said of the process of actually doing so, she added. “We found that people were put off by the prospect of budget contributions or any threat of joining the Euro and also simply by the process itself – there is significant voter exhaustion on this topic,” she said, citing research Persuasion conducted with a pro-EU think tank. ‘A lot of trauma’ Until now, the “reset” has yielded few tangible outcomes aside from an agreement for Britain to rejoin the Erasmus student exchange program next year, at a much higher cost than it paid previously. Burnham says these agreements could add up to 0.4% of GDP to the British economy and remove bureaucratic hurdles for food exporters. But Europe Minister Hamish Falconer conceded to the BBC that their implementation would compel the UK to accept EU regulations on products without being able to shape them. It echoes the old trade-off – sovereignty versus frictionless trade – which underpinned the fractious yearslong Brexit debate, the legacy of which hangs over whatever Burnham’s government decides to do next and Europe’s own moves. Indeed, the bloc’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said last week that the EU had suffered “a lot of trauma” from Britain’s departure before warning that any future negotiations “will not be that easy.”

articles.title: SBI freezes 19-year-old YouTuber's account over three Rs 1,000 Google transactions, fails to prove illegality, Jodhpur consumer commission orders bank to unfreeze it and pay Rs 15,000 compensation
articles.summary: JODHPUR: After freezing a 19-year-old YouTuber’s savings account over three Google transactions of Rs 1,000 each, State Bank of India (SBI) has been
articles.body: JODHPUR: After freezing a 19-year-old YouTuber’s savings account over three Google transactions of Rs 1,000 each, State Bank of India (SBI) has been directed by a Jodhpur consumer commission to unfreeze the account and pay him Rs 15,000, after failing to establish that the transactions were illegal.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I, Jodhpur, comprising chairperson Rajkumar Sudhar and member Dilshad Ali, passed the order on a complaint filed by Arjun, a resident of Nevra in Osian tehsil.Arjun had opened a savings account at SBI’s Nevra Road branch to receive earnings from his YouTube channel. He alleged that the bank flagged three transactions of Rs 1,000 each, made through Google on May 19, 2023, to promote his channel, and subsequently froze his account, leaving him unable to withdraw his money.SBI contended that Arjun had opened the account as a student and that its off-site transaction monitoring system detected suspicious transfers soon after. The bank said it had issued notices seeking an explanation but froze the account on May 31, 2023, after receiving no satisfactory response.The commission, however, observed that SBI failed to produce sufficient evidence to establish that the transactions were illegal or that Arjun was involved in any unlawful activity. It also noted that the bank could not establish that the notices had been properly communicated to him.Holding the account freeze to be a deficiency in service, the commission directed SBI to complete the KYC formalities and lift the freeze within two months, allowing Arjun to operate the account normally.It also ordered the bank to pay him Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.Stay updated with the latest Jodhpur news. articles.title: Texas inmate's execution takes over an hour as prison staff struggle to find suitable veins
articles.summary: Texas inmate Reinaldo Dennes repeatedly cried out in pain as prison staff struggled for over an hour to establish IV access for his lethal injection.
articles.body: A Texas inmate's execution lasted more than an hour Thursday as prison staff struggled to find suitable veins for a lethal injection, with the condemned man repeatedly complaining of severe pain before being pronounced dead. Reinaldo Dennes, who was convicted of capital murder in the 1996 killing of Houston diamond dealer Janos Szucs, repeatedly cried out during the procedure at the state penitentiary in Huntsville, according to The Associated Press. Dennes was pronounced dead at 7:08 p.m., one minute after the procedure was completed. The procedure lasted 63 minutes from the time Dennes was strapped to the gurney until its completion, as prison staff struggled to find suitable veins for the intravenous needles used to administer pentobarbital. CHRISTA PIKE'S EXECUTION DOCTOR SAYS MISPLACED IV SENT LETHAL DRUGS INTO HER ARMS INSTEAD OF VEINS The execution comes amid renewed scrutiny of lethal injection procedures following a failed execution attempt in Tennessee in September involving death row inmate Christa Pike, who survived two doses of pentobarbital that her attorneys said did not properly enter her bloodstream, causing serious injuries. Dennes repeatedly complained of pain after Thursday's procedure began, groaning and calling out to God, according to witnesses cited by the AP. "The pain! Go! Go!" Dennes exclaimed. "My right leg is killing me!" he later shouted, describing the sensation as a cramp. "I don't think this is normal. Take me, father. Don't let me suffer like this. C'mon," he added. CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEYS SAY SHE'S IN CRITICAL CONDITION AFTER BOTCHED LETHAL INJECTIONS Texas Department of Criminal Justice spokesperson Amanda Hernandez said all procedures were followed appropriately but acknowledged that staff made multiple unsuccessful attempts to establish IV access before placing needles in Dennes' left foot and the left side of his neck. Hernandez said she did not know how many attempts were unsuccessful but maintained that the locations ultimately used complied with the state's execution procedures. She also suggested that Dennes may have exaggerated his discomfort, noting that he complained of pain before the drugs began flowing and in areas where no IV had been placed. According to the AP, when asked whether Dennes was faking his pain, she replied, "I think, yeah, there were allegations ... There was nothing abnormal on our part." INDIANA, FLORIDA AND ALABAMA CARRY OUT RARE US TRIPLE EXECUTION DAY "This isn't the first time we had to insert IVs into other locations. It's also not the first time we've had an inmate make allegations of pain immediately," Hernandez said. Dennes was the second person executed in the United States on Thursday, following Florida's execution of Thomas Mitchell Overton, 71, who was convicted of killing a pregnant woman and her husband during a home invasion. Overton's execution marked Florida's 20th of the year, a state record, according to the AP. Fox News Digital has reached out to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice for additional comment. articles.title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad
articles.summary: The properties are marketed at premium prices with claims of “government-backed” returns, the BBC finds.
articles.body:
"This building is hell on Earth," says Phil, describing the black mould and rats at Castleview House, the block of flats in Runcorn, Cheshire, where he lives.

But to an estate agent called Britské Reality - which translates as British Real Estate - working with investors hundreds of miles away in the Czech Republic, the flat Phil rents through his benefits was an exciting business opportunity.

The estate agent's marketing material said the flat was a government-funded source of income for investors, where tenants were taken care of and the property was in excellent condition.

A Czech investor bought it last year for £163,150, more than double the £75,000 cost of similar apartments in the block.

The BBC has found more than 40 companies marketing similar properties to individuals in the UK and abroad, as businesses seek to profit from a government system intended to provide housing and support for vulnerable people.

About a dozen of these companies work with a property developer called Lee Jones, whose company sold Phil's flat.

The homes they are selling to investors are advertised as supported accommodation, a type of housing for people with issues including mental health problems or drug abuse issues, as well as people fleeing domestic violence.

Providers offering what is known as supported exempt accommodation are allowed to charge the taxpayer more than the usual housing benefit cap, because they have higher running costs. Tenants are entitled to care, support and supervision - although how much support should be provided is not defined.

While there are legitimate providers helping people back into independent living, the BBC has previously reported on how some are exploiting the system by taking the higher housing benefit payments but failing to provide support .

Our latest investigation found companies marketing supported housing properties to people in Hong Kong, Macau, Nigeria, Turkey, the Netherlands, the UK and other countries as a "secure", "government-backed" investment.

We also found adverts made misleading promises about the quality of the accommodation and support, with tenants saying they were receiving little or no care, while we observed examples of poor quality, unsafe accommodation.

Housing charities and experts have told the BBC the sector has been transformed into a profit-generating machine at the expense of some tenants' safety, care, and dignity.

Labour MP Abena Oppong-Asare, who chairs the Housing Select Committee, said it was "outrageous" that supported housing properties were being marketed as investments "particularly where there's public funds involved".

The BBC's findings were "alarming" and showed a sector "open to abuse", she added.

Lee Jones's company The Investment Room converted Castleview House in 2019 from an office block into more than 200 residential flats, including the one where Phil now lives.

Then Jones partnered with Nurture Housing Association. His company granted Nurture a 25-year-lease on some of the flats, to provide housing for people on government benefits. Jones has a close business relationship with Nurture's chief executive Chris Smith, with the pair also acting as joint directors of other housing companies.

Jones then worked with estate agents, which marketed the housing to investors in the UK and overseas using the regular cashflow generated by the 25-year lease with Nurture and the promise of government funding to justify inflated prices.

Lee Jones and Nurture have repeated this with property developments across England, including in Doncaster, Rotherham, Stockton-on-Tees and Bradford. These type of properties are also in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland but are funded and regulated differently.

Because neither profit-making private companies nor individuals can act as supported housing providers themselves, co-operation between developers, investors and publicly funded providers has become common.

The Czech marketing material found by the BBC said Nurture provides housing for people with mental health issues who receive the "aftercare program pursuant to Section 117 of the Mental Health Act", meaning they have been sectioned and discharged from hospital with a detailed care plan.

But Phil says he has never been sectioned under the Mental Health Act.

He does have severe depression and anxiety, and he is currently out of work. But he says he has never had any support or care, or met anyone working for Nurture during his time at the flat.

"Whoever marketed this property, the way they've worded it is total dishonesty," says Phil. "If they're looking to make as much profit as they can, then they clearly have no plans to fix the issues in the building."

Phil had no idea the flat he rents had been sold to overseas investors in May 2025 until the BBC contacted him. But there were clues: bills addressed to someone called Jan Hála had been coming through the letterbox for months.

Lee Jones told us that the properties his companies provide are "good quality accommodation" and he has no responsibility for the communal areas of Castleview House since he sold the freehold in 2021. He denied his relationship with Chris Smith amounted to a conflict of interest, but did not respond to questions about his role in marketing the properties.

Jan Hála, the Czech investor who now owns Phil's flat, and the Britské Reality estate agency did not respond to requests for comment.

We spoke to several other people living in flats run by Nurture Housing Association in Castleview House who said they were in supported accommodation. They reported receiving little or no help from Nurture but were afraid to speak out publicly for fear of eviction and becoming homeless.

There is also evidence that marketing materials for investors buying flats in Castleview were misleading. Investors were told Nurture was providing "specialist supported housing" - a claim which is repeated on its website.

According to the Regulator of Social Housing, this would mean it was providing a high level of care, equivalent to living in a care home.

But Nurture had not been registered as a specialised supported housing provider, the regulator said, and its claim to be providing this was "shocking".

In a statement, Nurture acknowledged that Castleview House is managed under a "general housing management model" and does not form part of its supported housing portfolio. It said it provided supported housing elsewhere through partners which were registered providers.

It said the Czech advert found by the BBC related to "historic marketing material" produced by third parties.

However, the BBC has seen marketing material from several other agents selling flats in Castleview House to investors, which also claim that Nurture is providing supported housing to the residents on a 25-year lease.

Nurture said it is not directly involved with the companies marketing the properties. But it said: "We will be reviewing communications with relevant agents and reminding them of the importance of ensuring that any information relating to Nurture is accurate, transparent and does not create misunderstanding regarding the accommodation or services provided."

While there are doubts about what kind of housing Nurture has been providing, the BBC also found other flats sold to investors overseas with tenants who were in supported exempt accommodation.

The web of companies involved in providing this housing and cross-border ownership means it can be difficult for vulnerable tenants to get help when there are problems with properties.

"The way that the current system works is there's different levels of involvement by different organisations and companies and no-one is directly accountable," Abena Oppong-Asare, the housing committee chairwoman, told us.

Mo, who has mental health issues, was housed in a studio flat in Cricklewood, north London, after he became homeless. The converted house containing his flat was bought by Gemelli London 2 Limited, a company run by French nationals living in the Czech Republic, for £1.83m in January last year.

He says his supported housing provider, Windrush Alliance, receives nearly £2,000 a month via Barnet Council for the flat. Mo says he receives £340 in universal credit for living expenses every month - but he is expected to pay Windrush a monthly £120 service charge out of that.

Last year his ceiling collapsed after a leak went unrepaired for more than a year and Mo was temporarily housed in another flat in the property.

Mo says his weekly visits from a Windrush support worker feel like a tick-box exercise and do not help him with the mental health issues which have been keeping him out of work.

Gemelli's director Stephane Boussier told the BBC that when the company bought the property "no complaints from residents were disclosed". It was made aware of issues in August 2025, he said, and since then has "raised them with Windrush in writing, inspected the property and pressed for them to be resolved".

He added that Gemelli London 2 Limited receives about £1,365 per flat per month from Windrush and does not receive any of the extra housing benefit that would be used for vulnerable tenants.

Windrush said it was aware of issues at Mo's property and was "working with the building owner to put them right". According to Gemelli, the ceiling was repaired after the BBC contacted the two companies.

Windrush has previously been criticised by the Regulator for Social Housing for a "failure to meet the standards" of the regulator, including failing to ensure "tenants are safe in their homes".

It acknowledged that it "fell short in the past". It wrote off £1.8m in "funds to former directors and companies under their control", saying the company's financial position had been "compromised" by their actions. The company now has a new board in place.

Windrush told us its "priority is residents, not investors" and the rates it charges "are agreed with the relevant local authorities" and "any surplus is reinvested in our homes and services".

In Bradford, the BBC visited City Exchange and Colonnade House, two former office blocks which Lee Jones has converted into housing - with Nurture Housing Association managing many of the flats.

Many of the properties there were advertised as supported housing investments. Residents showed us cockroach infestations, faulty fire alarms, broken lifts, leaks through the ceiling and black mould.

Nurture Housing said it was only responsible for the individual homes that it manages and does not manage communal areas or "wider building infrastructure".

"Nurture Housing and its managing agents regularly raise these concerns with the block manager," the company said.

The freeholder for Phil's block, Castleview House, and City Exchange, blamed "defects" by the developer Lee Jones for the problems with the buildings and said it was taking legal action. Colonnade House has had several building management companies in recent years and the latest said it was addressing the problems.

None of these companies or individuals are breaking the law, but critics say they are exploiting a lack of regulation in the sector.

Three years after the Supported Housing Act was passed in England, which would put in place a licensing regime for supported housing providers and give local councils more powers to shut down providers that failed to meet the standards, it still has not been implemented.

"It's taken too long," said Jasmine Basran, head of policy and campaigns at housing charity Crisis. "In the meantime, this an area where we've seen the worst kind of exploitation."

Additional reporting by Lorna Acquah and Abi Smitton
