articles.title: Andy Serkis backs 'admirable' Marlow Studios plan
articles.summary: The Gollum and Ian Dury actor says the studio will help boost local skills.
articles.body:
Film actor and director Andy Serkis has voiced his support for the "admirable" plans for Marlow Studios.

The Planet of the Apes and Lord of the Rings star had been a vocal supporter of the 90-acre film studio which will be built on green belt land in Buckinghamshire.

He highlighted its proximity to the National Film and Television School in nearby Beaconsfield as a major benefit for industry training.

"It's going to bring talent, it's going to bring business, it's going to bring skills, but it's also going to be a place of learning," said Serkis.

"I just think it's such an admirable operation. I really do."

Serkis explained that the UK film and television industry was "in such a great place at the moment" and the studio could bring skills and talent to nearby residents.

The development will include 18 sound stages and is expected to create about 2,060 permanent on-site jobs.

It was initially rejected by Buckinghamshire Council over concerns it was inappropriate for green belt land, but later granted planning permission after an appeal .

Serkis, who also played Ian Dury in the Sex & Drugs & Rock & Roll biopic , said: "It seems to be taking a piece of land which is, you know, brown land.

"It couldn't really be used for anything else. Admittedly it's on the green belt, but even so, it's not farmable land.

"The design of it is extraordinary, because it really will fit in kind of on the eco level so brilliantly."

articles.title: Missing fishing boat Kilda recovered from waters off Orkney
articles.summary: The Kilda and its three crew were reported missing near Lewis on 13 October.
articles.body:
A fishing boat that went missing near the Isle of Lewis a month ago has been recovered after it was spotted semi-submerged in the North Sea off Orkney.

Three men were on board the Kilda when it disappeared on 13 October.

The body of crew member Douglas Craigie was found by search teams the following day but two other men - Norman Murray and Murdo Morrison - are still missing.

The wreck was spotted east of Orkney on Wednesday morning, and a specialist vessel recovered from about 40 miles (64km) out to sea on Thursday before bringing it to Kirkwall.

The Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has started an investigation into the loss of the Kilda.

It is understood it will be kept in a secure yard while investigations are carried out.

Insp Neil Taylor, from Police Scotland, said: "Our thoughts remain with everyone affected by this tragic incident.

"The vessel recovered has been confirmed as the FV Kilda and we will continue to work with partners, including the MAIB, Maritime and Coastguard Agency, as well as local maritime experts, as our enquiries continue."

He said it was a very difficult time for the families and local community, and asked for patience while a full examination of the vessel was carried out.

"This will be a complex operation and we would ask that officers and specialists are given the time and space to carry out their enquiries," he added.

An HM Coastguard aircraft had confirmed the sighting of a semi-submerged boat on Wednesday.

Local firm Leask Marine was able to recover the Kilda in tricky conditions at about 18:00 on Thursday then brought the vessel into Kirkwall.

It was a cold, sombre scene when it arrived just before 23:00.

The Kilda was partly covered by a tarpaulin, but its name and its registration number were clearly visible. Two police officers went on board briefly with torches, then watched as it was lifted.

BBC Scotland understands part of the wheelhouse had been torn off and the rudder was gone, but the boat was still floating.

The Kilda was recovered about 200 miles (322km), in a straight line, from where it went missing.

One theory is that the vessel may have floated round the north coast of Orkney before being blown back south.

Earlier this month, an empty life raft from the Kilda washed up 200 miles away in Shetland .

The Kilda was last known to be operating close to the Port of Ness in Lewis.

Coastguard personnel, lifeboat crews, police and volunteers have been involved in searches since its disappearance.

A specialist Northern Lighthouse Board ship was brought in to carry out surveys of the seabed off north Lewis, and it identified two sites which were searched but nothing was found.

Speaking at the time of the Kilda's disappearance, Duncan Macinnes, secretary of the Western Isles Fishermen's Association, said the incident has had a devastating impact in the local community.

He told BBC Scotland: "It is just an unimaginable tragedy that happened just over a week ago and we have heartfelt sorrow for the grieving families who have suffered such loss and we pray that Tam and Murdo will be found.

"We are thankful for the rescue services that have taken place by the Coastguard, the Marine Accident Investigation Branch, Police Scotland, and all the others that have gone and assisted in any way possible to try and find those that have been lost.

"With a tragedy like this which is one of the worst fishing tragedies that we have experienced in the Western Isles in a generation, it is going to leave broken hearts.

"It is just very difficult and total devastation for the industry and for the community."

Ness is a sparsely populated area on the northern tip of Lewis.

It is an area of rugged coastline, with many of its roughly 1,300 people living in crofting townships - small holdings where families can raise livestock and grow crops while working other jobs.

The parish has one of the highest concentrations of Gaelic speakers in the Western Isles.

A minute's silence was held at the Royal National Mòd, Scotland's annual celebration of Gaelic culture and language, which was taking place in Glasgow at the time.

Flowers were also left on the plinth of the Ness Fishery Memorial at Port of Ness.

articles.title: Wildlife conservation cash targets Yorkshire ex-colliery sites
articles.summary: The project aims to create and restore habitats for amphibians and lizards at sites in Yorkshire.
articles.body:
Ponds are to be restored and freshwater habitats created for amphibians and reptiles at two former colliery sites in South Yorkshire.

The Froglife charity has been awarded nearly £890,000 of Lottery cash to carry out the work in Rother Valley, as well as at sites in North and West Yorkshire.

Kiveton and Dinnington Community Woodlands were originally regenerated through the National Coalfields Programme after the pits there closed in the 1990s.

Sheila Grundry, from Froglife, said staff were "delighted" to work in the area because "freshwater will make a lasting difference for frogs and other wildlife and it's a great way for local people to learn new skills".

The £889,761 investment in Froglife's Coalface to Wildspace project will also help local communities connect with nature, according to the charity.

The aim of the project across Yorkshire is to create 48 new ponds, improve 93 existing freshwater habitats and establish new "neighbourhood wildlife corridors" like small ponds and bug hotels.

These "corridors" will act as stepping stones for local wildlife from insects to birds, providing food, shelter and water to improve biodiversity across former industrial sites and help wildlife move between one habitat and another.

Conservationist Andy Goff, project manager in Yorkshire, said the transformation of the sites would be for everyone.

"We want people to engage with the nature that is on their doorstep and wildlife in general," he explained.

"I'm really excited about getting people involved from all over Yorkshire."

The Coalface to Wildspace project is funded by The National Lottery Heritage Fund for the next four years, with Froglife having already run similar projects in the Midlands and Scotland.

Rother Valley MP Jake Richards said the project was important for the area.

"These former industrial sites are an important part of our area's history," he said.

"This project will help transform them into thriving habitats while creating opportunities for local people to get involved."

articles.summary: RAIPUR: Holding an insurance company guilty of deficiency in service for rejecting a policyholder’s medical insurance claim, the District Consumer
articles.body: RAIPUR: Holding an insurance company guilty of deficiency in service for rejecting a policyholder’s medical insurance claim, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Raipur, has directed the insurer to reimburse Rs 1,78,295 spent on medical treatment, besides paying compensation of Rs 10,000 for mental agony and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.The commission held that the insurance company could not subsequently rely on the alleged non-disclosure of medical conditions without establishing that the policyholder had concealed material information.Referring to the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in Om Prakash Agrawal versus Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd., the commission observed that an insurer cannot reject a claim merely by alleging suppression of a pre-existing disease without establishing the relevant facts.The commission held that the insurer's conduct amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The commission, comprising president Prashant Kundu and member Dr Anand Verma, passed the order on Nov 3, in a complaint filed by Bholanath Agrawal, a resident of Dhamtari district, against Max Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd.According to the complaint, Agrawal and his wife were covered under a Mediclaim policy issued by the insurance company for the period Sept 4, 2018, to Sept 3, 2019. The policy provided medical coverage of up to Rs 10 lakh against a premium of Rs 61,925.Agrawal was admitted to a private hospital in Raipur on Dec 22, 2018, for treatment and was discharged on Dec 26, 2018. He incurred medical expenses of Rs 1,78,295.When the hospital sought cashless treatment approval, the insurance company rejected the request on Dec 22, 2018, citing the policyholder's alleged pre-existing medical conditions, including diabetes and hypertension, and the need for further verification of his medical history.The insurer subsequently issued a repudiation letter on Feb 27, 2019, maintaining that the medical records and investigations showed that the policyholder had been suffering from the ailments before the commencement of the policy and had not disclosed the relevant medical history while submitting the proposal form.The company also contended that the policyholder had a history of coronary artery bypass surgery in 2014 and had failed to disclose material information relating to his health. It maintained that the claim was rejected in accordance with the policy's terms and conditions and that there was no deficiency in service.However, the commission, after examining the pleadings, affidavits, medical records, insurance documents and other evidence, found that the insurer had failed to establish that the policyholder had deliberately concealed material facts while obtaining the insurance policy.The commission observed that the insurer had issued the policy after receiving the proposal form and relevant medical examination reports, including pathology and other investigation reports. It noted that the company had been provided an opportunity to examine the proposal and the medical documents before issuing the policy.It further observed that the policyholder had undergone medical investigations before the policy was issued and the insurer had accepted the proposal after assessing the documents.The commission also examined the circumstances surrounding the rejection of the cashless treatment request and the subsequent repudiation of the claim. It noted that the policyholder had been admitted to hospital for treatment and that the insurance company had rejected the cashless facility on the basis of its assessment of his medical history.It partly allowed the complaint under Section 12 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.The commission directed the insurer to pay Rs 1,78,295 towards the medical expenses incurred by the complainant within 45 days of the order. It also directed the company to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses within the same period.The commission further ordered that if the insurer failed to pay the awarded amount within 45 days, it would have to pay the amount along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum until payment.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Raipur | Silver Rate in Raipur | Bank Holidays in Raipur | Public Holidays in Raipur | Raipur AQI | Weather in Raipur | Petrol Price in Raipur | Diesel Price in Raipur | CNG Price in Raipur | LPG Price in RaipurStay updated with the latest Raipur news. articles.title: For Xi and Putin, the Trump trilateral was a win for a new world order
articles.summary: From an airy government villa in the hills of southern China on Thursday emerged an image, perhaps, for our times: the leaders of China, Russia and the US standing shoulder-to-shoulder, proclaiming themselves the stewards of world peace.
articles.body: From an airy government villa in the hills of southern China on Thursday emerged an image, perhaps, for our times: the leaders of China, Russia and the US standing shoulder-to-shoulder, proclaiming themselves the stewards of world peace. For Trump, the moment was a well-timed photo-op – a diplomatic flex for a president who revels in such spectacle and whose party is reeling from a major loss in the US midterm elections. But for Xi and Putin, the meeting is more likely to go down as a vindication of their vision that the world is undergoing a fundamental rebalancing of power – in their favor. In opening remarks before the roughly 90-minute meeting between them, Trump said he was honored to sit next to the two and framed the trio – the world’s three largest nuclear powers – as uniquely placed to work together for a “safer future.” “No problems were ever solved under the old school, refusing to talk about them,” said Trump. “Together, we are choosing a different course.” But for talks that ended with a handful of vaguely worded outcomes – and no evidence that the US president and commander-in-chief of the world’s most powerful military had tried to hold Putin to account for his illegal invasion of Ukraine – that “different course” appears to be one that plays to the objectives of Moscow and Beijing. Xi and Putin have long looked to push back against a world order they see as unfairly dominated by the US and its values. A brief exchange caught on camera in 2023 during a state visit by the Chinese leader to Moscow captures that ambition. There, as he shook Putin’s hand, Xi was heard saying: “Together, we should push forward these changes that have not happened for 100 years.” To that end, they have tightened their own partnership and built out non-Western international blocs engineered to help usher in a “multipolar” order that favors their interests. For Xi and Putin, all this is underpinned by a shared view: that the East is rising as the West declines – and the age of American superpower comes to an end. And what better illustration of that shift than sitting around a table in China’s futuristic tech hub of Shenzhen with a US president hailing them both as friends? A new world order Headlines across Chinese state media the day after the summit were in no doubt about its significance. The state’s lead news agency hailed the meeting as a “new starting point” for a “new model of relationship among major powers.” That new model, explained the article, is one based on “mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, dialogue and consultation.” For China’s leadership, those are buzzwords key to the country’s unimpeded rise on the global stage, essentially insurance that the US won’t look to meddle in what Beijing sees as its business – especially when it comes to its territorial claims on the self-ruling and democratic island of Taiwan. And during the summit, with Trump to his left and Putin to his right, Xi pressed that point, using that time, according to Chinese media, to spell out China’s conditions for the three to get along. At the top of that list? “Respect one another’s sovereignty and territorial integrity” – and stay out of one another’s internal affairs. For Putin, the meeting was yet another assurance that Trump is taking his concerns into consideration as the US president looks to end Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Speaking about Trump after the meeting, Putin said, “we have shared certain commonalities in our approaches regarding so-called civilizational values.” That too, is a buzzword embraced by Putin and Xi, whose vision for a new world order is not one of countries holding each other accountable to universal standards governing rights and political freedoms, but one where countries – and autocrats – are able to set their own rules for their people. The two leaders will of course be well aware of changing political tides in the US – and the potential that a new Congress in January and a new American president in 2029 could bring immense change to American foreign policy. Xi and Putin – both shrewd operators who have dominated their countries’ politics for years – will too have calculated they are unlikely to again see another American president as amenable to their interests as Trump. But that’s what is likely to give this moment even more momentum, as both sides play up the win – and continue their push to reshape global power.

articles.title: UP CM Yogi Adityanath’s mother Savitri Devi passes away at 91 in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: Savitri Devi, the mother of Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, died at the age of 91 at her ancestral home in Pauri Garhwal district
articles.body: DEHRADUN: Savitri Devi, the mother of Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, died at the age of 91 at her ancestral home in Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand on Friday morning.Yogi Adityanath's brother Mahendra confirmed the news, saying she had been experiencing breathing difficulties and passed away at 11.50 am.According to news agency PTI, despite receiving the news of his mother's demise, Adityanath continued with his address to people in Gorakhpur on Friday. Setting aside his personal grief, he addressed people in the city and went ahead with his programmes focused on youth welfare and public service.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami condoled her death in a post on X, describing the news as "deeply saddening and heartbreaking"."The news of the passing of Smt. Savitri Devi Ji, the revered mother of Uttar Pradesh’s respected chief minister, Shri Yogi Adityanath Ji, is deeply saddening and heartbreaking.""A mother’s affection, blessings, and tender love are life’s most precious treasures. Her passing is an irreparable loss for the family. I pray to Baba Kedarnath to grant the departed soul a place at His divine feet and to give Hon’ble Yogi Ji and all the grieving family members the strength to bear this immense sorrow," Dhami said.Union minister of state for finance Pankaj Chaudhary took to social media platform X to express his condolences."The passing of Smt. Savitri Devi Ji, the revered mother of Uttar Pradesh's Hon'ble Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath Ji, is deeply saddening and heart-wrenching. A mother's departure from this world is a loss in life that can never be made up for," he said.Expressing solidarity with the chief minister and his family, Chaudhary added, "In this difficult hour of grief, my deepest condolences are with the Hon'ble Chief Minister and all the bereaved family members. I pray to Lord Shri Ram to grant the departed soul a place at His divine feet and give the Hon'ble CM and all family members the strength to bear this immense grief. Om Shanti."Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Hours after Trump reportedly says ‘tired’ Putin is ready for a deal, Ukraine hit with massive strikes
articles.summary: Russia launched a deadly attack on Ukraine overnight into Friday, just hours after President Vladimir Putin met his US and Chinese counterparts for historic trilateral talks in which the three powers billed themselves as a force for peace in the world.
articles.body: Russia launched a deadly attack on Ukraine overnight into Friday, just hours after President Vladimir Putin met his US and Chinese counterparts for historic trilateral talks in which the three powers billed themselves as a force for peace in the world. Trump spoke with European leaders after the call, reportedly describing Putin as “tired” and ready for peace. But Kyiv said Russia fired at least 110 missiles overnight - an unusually large number even amid Russia’s frequent aerial assaults. Eight people have been killed and at least 28 injured during the missile and drone attack which has so far lasted more than ten hours, according to Ukrainian authorities. Some 400 drones, including 120 jet-powered drones which are essentially compact cruise missiles, were part of the attack. The Polish government said fighter jets were scrambled and Patriot air defense systems activated early on Friday after Poland’s airspace was violated during the attack, with “objects” flying in and falling inside the country’s territory. The deadly assault came hours after Putin left China following a day of meetings in Shenzhen with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The talks failed to produce any breakthrough in Moscow’s more than four-year war in Ukraine, and appeared to be used by Putin as an opportunity to repeat his maximalist demands in front of a global audience. The Russian leader hailed the summit as historic and told reporters the discussions took place in a “relaxed and very intimate atmosphere.” In his opening remarks, Putin said Russia, China and the US had “shared interests” in settling the Ukraine war. No official declaration was released after the talks, but Trump did later speak with the so-called Coalition of the Willing, a group of Ukraine’s key allies, which was convening in Berlin with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. According to a senior European official with knowledge of the call’s contents, the president’s main message was that “Putin is tired, wants to end this, ready for a deal.” The official said Trump’s suggestion was “to reach out and grasp at the opportunity.” He said the Europeans were “constructive in response but want proof.” Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who was part of the call, said Trump sounded “fairly optimistic,” but he words were received “very cautiously in the room.” “I don’t hide the fact that I’ve heard this very often from President Trump. His belief in Putin’s goodwill seems unshakable, even though so far there are no facts to support it,” he said, adding that it “would be good, if it really turned out that Russia was genuinely ready to engage in peace talks.” Kushner said Trump had conveyed a “very strong message” to both Xi and Putin about his desire for peace and would like “to engage both of them very aggressively to get there.” Strikes target key bridges Russia’s defense ministry said in a post to Telegram it launched a “massive strike using high-precision weapons from land, sea, and air,” as well as drones, targeting Ukrainian military and energy facilities, port infrastructure in the Odesa region, and transport infrastructure in Kyiv. But Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said “absolutely all the targets were ordinary civilian infrastructure – things that literally sustain people’s lives.” “This was one of the largest attacks. The strike tactics were particularly vicious this time: several groups of missiles were launched, with pauses of 20 to 30 minutes between them to make it harder to put out fires, clear rubble, and carry out repairs,” Zelensky said. Zelensky said that 27 of the missiles Russia fired overnight were ballistic. According to the Ukrainian Air Force, only three were intercepted, reflecting Ukraine’s critical shortage of missiles for it US-made Patriot air defense system. Earlier, Ukraine said Moscow’s targets included a hospital in Kharkiv and residential buildings in the Dnipropetrovsk, Lviv, Vinnytsia, Sumy, and Chernihiv regions. Three of Kyiv’s bridges were damaged in the overnight strikes, according to mayor Vitaly Klitschko, halting transport links connecting the two sides of the capital. “All emergency services have done and will continue to do everything possible to mitigate the consequences of the attack as quickly as possible,” Klitschko said, adding that people should avoid traveling if possible. The deadly attack came after Putin vowed revenge for Ukraine’s recent attacks on prized project, the strategic multibillion-dollar bridge linking Russia with the occupied Crimea. “There will be no negotiations,” he said. “I believe our response, as I have just said, will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge.” The attacks have also knocked down power in several regions across Ukraine, just as temperatures are beginning to drop to bellow zero. Several districts in Kyiv were without power due to the attack, according to energy company DTEK. Emergency power outages have also been implemented in the Lviv, Zakarpattia, and Ivano-Frankivsk regions, according to Ukrenergo, the country’s state-owned electricity operator, which called the situation in the power grid “extremely critical.”

articles.title: FBI arrests Georgia man accused of sending cryptocurrency to ISIS-linked individuals and groups
articles.summary: Georgia man Younes Moustafa Younes faces federal charges for allegedly sending more than $26,000 to ISIS affiliates, the Department of Justice announced.
articles.body: A Georgia man is facing federal charges after allegedly sending more than $26,000 to individuals and groups affiliated with ISIS, the Department of Justice (DOJ) announced. Younes Moustafa Younes, 34, of Lavonia, Georgia, was charged with one count of international money laundering and one count of destruction of evidence, according to the DOJ. Younes was arrested Nov. 18 and made his initial appearance Thursday in federal court. Federal prosecutors allege Younes altered and destroyed evidence leading up to his arrest. During a search of his apartment, FBI agents discovered three cellphones submerged in an unknown solution, including one that had been smashed and another with its identification number removed, according to the criminal complaint. FBI ARRESTS 3 MEN WHO ALLEGEDLY PLEDGED ALLEGIANCE TO ISIS, FUNDED DRONE ATTACKS TARGETING US TROOPS OVERSEAS Investigators also found shredded documents submerged in an unknown solution inside a bathtub. According to the complaint, Younes sent approximately $16,807 through cryptocurrency transactions between December 2025 and June 2026, using multiple phone numbers and accounts allegedly intended to conceal his identity. Investigators say at least some of the funds were intended to support ISIS operations in Syria. Prosecutors also allege that Younes sent approximately $9,206 through 11 cryptocurrency transactions between December 2021 and April 2022, using an alias to conceal his involvement. NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS The FBI first identified Younes in 2020 after he allegedly accessed ISIS propaganda online, according to the complaint. During an interview with law enforcement, Younes acknowledged viewing the material but denied supporting extremist ideologies. Prosecutors allege he later became increasingly radicalized, expressing support for ISIS and other terrorist figures through encrypted communications. If convicted, Younes faces up to 20 years in federal prison on each charge, according to the Justice Department. The international money laundering charge also carries a potential fine of up to $500,000, while the destruction of evidence charge carries a potential fine of up to $250,000. articles.title: A year before Apollo 13’s oxygen tank exploded, NASA engineer Arturo Campos had drafted an emergency power plan; it helped bring the crew home
articles.summary: Discover how NASA engineer Arturo Campos's foresight and emergency power plan played a crucial role in bringing the Apollo 13 crew home safely after a life-threatening oxygen tank explosion.
articles.body: Imagine being woken at home by a phone call that changes everything. That's what happened to Arturo Campos on 13 April 1970. According to NASA's profile of Campos, he was sleeping when colleagues at the Manned Spacecraft Center, now Johnson Space Center, called him in. An oxygen tank on Apollo 13 had ruptured. Three astronauts were stranded in a damaged spacecraft about 320,000 km (200,000 miles) away from Earth. Campos was the engineer who had drawn up a plan for exactly this kind of emergency.A plan nobody had tested The blast cut off electricity, light and water in the command module. The Moon landing was abandoned, and the top priority became getting James Lovell, Jack Swigert and Fred Haise home alive. Before the mission, the team had prepared a backup plan. This plan involved shifting the power from the lunar module, which was designed to land on the Moon, to the command module. The agency’s profile adds that the plan had never been tested. Campos was the electrical power subsystem manager of the lunar module. He went to the Mission Evaluation Room and rewrote the plan on the spot for the damaged spacecraft. NASA quotes him as saying he had written procedures for that situation a year before.From a mechanic’s son to NASA engineerCampos was born in Laredo, Texas, in 1934 to a Mexican-American family. At the time, it wasn't common for Hispanic students to go for engineering degrees. At first, Campos wasn't even aiming for college, thinking of becoming a car mechanic like his father. His high school chemistry and physics teacher, Josephine Baird, saw the potential in him and encouraged him to take classes while working at his father's garage. He attended Laredo Junior College and earned a degree in electrical engineering from the University of Texas in 1956. He later supervised aircraft maintenance at Kelly Air Force Base before joining NASA in the early 1960s. There, he became one of the go-to figures behind the electrical system of the Apollo lunar modules, including the one used for the first Moon landing in 1969.Fifteen hours and a lifeboat The plan took about 15 hours to carry out. Enough power moved from the lunar module to the emergency batteries in the command module to provide heat for the crew, get them home and allow them to land safely. It was part of a much larger rescue mission. As described by NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, mission control declared the command module mortally wounded less than two hours after Swigert’s transmission, with only 15 minutes of power left. The crew moved to the lunar module, which served as a lifeboat, and spent three and a half days there. Its provisions had been planned for two astronauts for one and a half days. Carbon dioxide levels became critical before the team managed to put square filters from the command module into round openings. With all the instruments turned off to conserve power, the temperature dropped to 38°F (3°C). The crew landed in the Pacific Ocean near Samoa on 17 April 1970.More than one night of work Campos is remembered as someone proud of his heritage. He was one of the few Mexican-American employees at Johnson, where most of the staff were white. He helped recruit more Hispanic workers to the space programme. He also helped start the League of United Latin American Citizens Council 660, a chapter of Mexican-American engineers at NASA that handed out scholarships to Hispanic students. In 1970, Richard Nixon awarded him, and other members of mission control, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Campos retired in 1980, continued consulting for Houston firms, and passed away in 2001 at age 66. His story shows how big rescues often begin with quiet planning long before anyone needs them.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Soaking storms shift north to Florida’s Space Coast and prompt water rescues
articles.summary: Storms that brought record rains to South Florida this week shifted north to the Space Coast on Thursday, sending rivers over their banks and prompting water rescues of people and horses alike.
articles.body: Storms that brought record rains to South Florida this week shifted north to the Space Coast on Thursday, sending rivers over their banks and prompting water rescues of people and horses alike. In California, rain continued to pound the coast, filling streets with water, submerging cars and prompting hundreds of delayed flights. This is supposed to be Florida’s dry season that runs from October to May. So far, it has been quite the opposite. “Never seen such a thing like this in Florida,” said Jazmin Foster, who has lived in her Melbourne home for eight years. The storms have already dumped nearly 17 inches of rain over 48 hours in the Fort Lauderdale area, according to preliminary totals from the National Weather Service. Places like Fort Lauderdale, Melbourne and West Palm Beach have already seen their wettest November on record, the National Weather Service said. This week’s storms have been fueled by persistent high pressure over Virginia and a low-pressure system and an associated stationary front in the Gulf, which together have pushed a steady onshore flow across the Florida Peninsula. Heavy rains and flash flooding were expected to persist through Friday, possibly moving north toward the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic into the weekend, the weather service said. Dozens of horses and other animals caught in floodwaters at equestrian center On Thursday, the storms hit Brevard County directly. People with trailers braved knee-deep water to rescue dozens of horses and other animals at the Blue Lake Equestrian Center, an animal hospice and boarding facility in Cocoa. The animals were taken to a dry pasture elsewhere. First responders conducted nearly 100 high-water rescues across the county, and those numbers continued to climb, Sheriff Wayne Ivey said. The city of Palm Bay conducted mandatory evacuations for some residents of a mobile home community. Shelters were opened for residents forced from their homes. Water inundated Foster’s home Thursday, two weeks after she endured a previous round of flooding. She said an insurance claim filed for the earlier flood was denied. “Where is FEMA? Multiple people here in Brevard need help! I know other people are worse than we are!” Foster told The Associated Press via social media. Nearly 200 Florida National Guard personnel with 50 high-water vehicles have been deployed to help, the Division of Emergency Management said. Other responding agencies included about 235 officers with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission. The St. Johns River near Cocoa rose above a record flood level set in 1953 and was forecast to stay at least 2 feet above flood stage through early next week, according to the weather service. Cyndy Paulin saw a fish swimming on her flooded street in Cocoa on Thursday, and her adventurous 5-year-old granddaughter played in the water. She brought a small body board and got on it, but it immediately sank to the ground, and she got soaked. “She had a blast,” Paulin said. El Niño isn’t going away anytime soon The storms are an offshoot of El Niño, the natural warming of the Pacific near the equator that warps weather patterns worldwide. Forecasters said El Niño conditions are expected to persist through the spring, meaning the soggy extreme weather in Florida and California will likely continue through the winter. “That’s what the forecast models are saying,” said Yale Climate Connections meteorologist Jeff Masters. “Winter hasn’t even come yet — we’re still in November. And things are likely to get even more active. And with record-warm ocean temperatures both off the coast of California and off the coast of Florida, we’re going to be seeing some very heavy downpours.” In July, United Nations officials warned that El Niño would add fuel to the world’s accelerating climate crisis, powered by the burning of coal, oil and natural gas. Longtime Pompano Beach resident Ken Evans said he has seen heavier rain and flooding worsen, especially over the past five years. On Tuesday night, he was caught in his SUV on Interstate 95 north of Miami during a heavy downpour with hail that left many roads under water. “This is absolutely a whole new cycle that’s going on, and a cycle that we should be very concerned about,” Evans said. California endures more flooding Preliminary totals showed one area of Los Angeles received more than 3 inches of rain during a 12-hour period ending Thursday, the weather service said. Some drivers were forced to abandon cars that stalled in floodwaters. More than 200 flights to and from Los Angeles International Airport were delayed Thursday, about 12% of the total air traffic, but there were only a handful of cancellations, according to Flightradar24. South of the Monterey Peninsula, rock and mud slides in Big Sur forced a more than 40-mile (64-kilometer) closure of Highway 1 along the Pacific coast. In West Oakland, Adriana Uchishiba woke up scared Wednesday after finding her bed floating in her room with floodwaters inside her house. A heater was still plugged in, and Uchishiba could feel the electrical currents in the water. A maintenance worker brought dehumidifiers and a water suction pump to remove the water, and Uchishiba hopes they acted quickly enough to avoid mold and mildew. Her friends have helped her clean up, taking her clothes to their homes to wash, but she and her roommate have to get new beds, blankets and books, she said. “If it wasn’t for my friends coming out and showing up ... this place would still be underwater,” she said. Watching the skies — and surf — for Thanksgiving week A nontropical low-pressure system expected to form Friday could become a subtropical or tropical storm along the southeastern U.S. coast, the National Hurricane Center in Miami said. The southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts should expect strong winds, dangerous surf and coastal flooding into early next week. In Southern California, the weather service said extremely high tides of more than 8 feet (2.4 meters) were expected to continue through next week.

articles.title: Pakistan minister visits India for first time since 2025 war
articles.summary: Islamabad and New Delhi insist the visit is strictly multilateral, despite hopes it could open a channel for contact.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan — Pakistan’s climate change minister, Musadik Malik, arrived in New Delhi on Friday, becoming the first Pakistani federal minister to visit India since the neighbours fought a four-day war in May 2025.

Malik is attending the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, a three-day gathering that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due to inaugurate on Friday evening. Malik is expected to address the forum on Saturday.

No bilateral meeting has been announced. Pakistan’s Foreign Office said on Thursday that its participation was “reflective of its contribution as an active SCO member State to promote dialogue, cooperation and understanding in line with ‘Shanghai Spirit’”.

It is the first such visit since then-Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari travelled to Goa in May 2023.

Both governments have framed these exchanges as routine SCO business.

With Pakistan due to host the bloc’s leaders next August, the question is how far contact confined to a multilateral forum can go — and whether this could set the stage for Modi to travel to Islamabad for the summit.

Indian media, quoting diplomatic sources, reported that India’s invitation was for Pakistan’s minister for national heritage and culture, Aurangzeb Khan Khichi.

Pakistan’s Foreign Office said on November 6 only that it had received an invitation and would decide after consultations. Islamabad has not said why it sent Malik.

The Foreign Office said Malik would “share Pakistan’s perspective on the salience of dialogue among civilisations” and meet SCO member states on the sidelines.

Jauhar Saleem, president of the Islamabad-based Institute of Regional Studies (IRS) and a former foreign secretary, said the choice was Pakistan’s to make.

“There is no hard and fast rule about who represents a country at such fora, and it is the prerogative of the invited state to nominate the representative it considers most appropriate,” he told Al Jazeera.

“Civilisation is not only about heritage and culture; it is about how societies relate to their land, their rivers, and one another,” Saleem added.

Khurram Dastgir Khan, a former federal minister for foreign affairs and defence and senior leader of the governing Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), said the choice was deliberate.

Sending a minister of its own choosing “lets Pakistan take part as an SCO member without being seen to buy into India’s framing or showcase,” he told Al Jazeera.

He said it also signalled Pakistan’s aim “to be seen as a constructive host for the 2027 summit; thereby nudging the door open an inch for PM Modi’s participation”.

Pakistan took over the SCO’s rotating chairmanship on September 1 and will host the leaders’ summit in Islamabad in August 2027, the month both countries mark 80 years of independence.

New Delhi has sought to keep the visit within a narrow SCO frame.

At an October 28 briefing, foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India had invited “all SCO members” “as per established practice”, along with dialogue partners and one observer.

Asked whether New Delhi was reviewing its Pakistan policy ahead of upcoming multilateral engagements, he said: “Post the Pahalgam attack, we have a Pakistan policy. That Pakistan policy remains in place; there has been no change.”

India blames Pakistan for the April 2025 attack in Pahalgam, in Indian-administered Kashmir, in which gunmen killed 26 civilians, setting the stage for the war that followed. Islamabad denies any involvement.

Sharat Sabharwal, India’s high commissioner to Pakistan from 2009 to 2013, said the invitation followed from India’s role as host.

“This is a meeting in the SCO framework, where India, as the organiser, has to invite all member countries. Therefore, at this juncture, there is no reason to look for any deeper meaning in this visit,” he told Al Jazeera.

Modi proposed the forum at last year’s SCO summit in Tianjin, China.

Irfan Nooruddin, a professor at Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service, said the initiative gave New Delhi a narrative of its own.

“If anything, it will be spun as further indication of India’s leading role in the region and its magnanimity in terms of including Pakistan in the dialogues,” he told Al Jazeera.

Rezaul Hasan Laskar, foreign affairs editor at The Hindustan Times newspaper in New Delhi, said there was little appetite at home for anything more.

“The government has maintained this is a multilateral engagement under the SCO framework, and that there will be no bilateral engagements with Pakistan till the issue of terrorism is addressed,” he told Al Jazeera. “There doesn’t appear to be widespread public backing for a fresh approach towards Pakistan.”

The SCO has been one of the few forums bringing the two countries together since they joined in 2017.

Bhutto-Zardari’s visit to Goa ended in public sparring. In his speech, he warned against “weaponising terrorism for diplomatic point scoring”, without naming India.

Jaishankar later described him to reporters as a “promoter, justifier and spokesperson of a terrorism industry”. The two did not hold a separate bilateral meeting.

Jaishankar’s subsequent visit to Islamabad in October 2024, for an SCO heads of government meeting, passed more quietly, with pleasantries but no talks.

In September this year, Alok Dimri, India’s SCO coordinator, spent three days in Islamabad and shook hands with Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. He described the visit to reporters as “an annual rotational ritual of the SCO”.

Dastgir said such contact had done little to change the course of relations.

“The Indian External Affairs Minister’s October 2024 trip to Islamabad for SCO proved a dead-end, despite the hoopla. It did not prevent open hostilities in May 2025,” he said.

Salman Bashir, a former Pakistani high commissioner to India, was blunter. “SCO is an opportunity to maintain a semblance of civility. Don’t think that it is a pathway to normalcy,” he told Al Jazeera.

Beyond the SCO calendar, nearly every bilateral link remains frozen.

India has held the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty “in abeyance” since the Pahalgam attack.

On August 31, a court of arbitration in The Hague ruled that India could not suspend the treaty unilaterally. New Delhi rejected the court’s jurisdiction.

In September, Indian and Pakistani naval vessels collided in the Arabian Sea, prompting India to summon Pakistan’s chargé d’affaires in protest. Neither country has had a high commissioner in the other’s capital since 2019.

Contact has continued below the official level.

Laskar pointed to “several Track 1.5 and Track 2 engagements right from a few months after the conflict in May last year,” referring to semi-official and unofficial meetings only partly involving government representation.

Pakistan’s chairmanship will bring a series of tests before next August.

At its summit in Bishkek, the SCO named Lahore its tourism and cultural capital for 2026-27. During his visit, Dimri said he hoped to see the city.

The biggest test will be the leaders’ summit itself. Indian officials have told local media that New Delhi will decide its level of representation closer to the date.

Laskar said a breakthrough was hard to predict, but such a visit “could be the pathway to opening all sorts of possibilities”.

Dastgir said SCO meetings “can provide the pretext for bilateral communication, however rudimentary. Sidelines encounters need no announcement and no concession.”

Nooruddin did not rule out a visit by Modi.

“If there’s a single leader in India’s context who could do that, and get away with it, it is he. A sort of Nixon goes to China , if you would,” he said.

“But, again, so much will happen between now and next August that prognosticating so far into the future is pretty pointless. Let’s just say that it’s entirely possible that Modi goes but I wouldn’t bet on it.”

articles.title: Arkansas prosecutors moved to seize a man's home in a drug case, but an appeals court compared its $127,967 purchase price with his $2,500 fine and ruled the forfeiture unconstitutional
articles.summary: A man convicted of possessing cocaine with intent to deliver faced the loss of his Arkansas home after prosecutors sought to seize the property in
articles.body: A man convicted of possessing cocaine with intent to deliver faced the loss of his Arkansas home after prosecutors sought to seize the property in connection with his drug offence. However, an appeals court has ruled that taking a house purchased for nearly $128,000 was an excessive punishment when the man had received a $2,500 fine and 10 years of supervised probation.In a November 18, 2026, decision available on Justia, the Arkansas Court of Appeals reversed and dismissed the forfeiture order against Richard Smith's property. The court found that although the house had a sufficient connection to the drug offence to qualify for forfeiture under state law, taking it would violate the Eighth Amendment's protection against excessive fines because the value of the property was grossly disproportionate to the seriousness of the offence.Drug investigation led to a forfeiture caseOn April 20, 2023, the state filed a notice of lis pendens and notice of forfeiture lien concerning Smith's property. A search of his home was conducted around April 23, during which officers discovered a safe containing multiple bags, 3.1626 grams of cocaine and several pills. Smith was subsequently arrested on drug-related charges. A warrant of seizure for forfeiture followed on April 27.Smith pleaded guilty on August 8, 2024, to possessing between 10 and 200 grams of cocaine with intent to deliver, a Class A felony, and possessing drug paraphernalia, a Class A misdemeanour. He was sentenced to 120 months of supervised probation, one day in jail with credit for time served, and a $2,500 fine.The state subsequently pursued the forfeiture of his house, arguing that the property had been used in connection with drug activity. At the August 14, 2025, forfeiture hearing, officers testified that they had observed increased traffic at the residence before the search. Some individuals leaving the property were later found carrying methamphetamine. However, the state crime laboratory report showed that cocaine was the only controlled substance recovered from the house that had been tested. Officers could not explain why the remaining substances had not been tested.Smith testified that the drugs were for personal use and acknowledged that he was a heavy drug user. Nevertheless, the circuit court found sufficient evidence to support forfeiture and ordered the property transferred to the Fifteenth Judicial District Prosecuting Attorney's Office.Why the appeals court found the forfeiture excessiveSmith challenged the forfeiture, arguing that the evidence connecting his home to drug sales was insufficient and that taking the property would violate the Eighth Amendment's Excessive Fines Clause. The Arkansas Court of Appeals agreed with his constitutional argument, although it rejected his challenge to the connection between the property and the offence. It explained that state law allowed real estate to be forfeited when it was used to facilitate certain serious drug offences. Smith's conviction was sufficient to establish the required connection.However, the court emphasised that a punitive forfeiture must remain proportionate to the seriousness of the underlying offence. Citing the US Supreme Court's decision in United States v. Bajakajian, it explained that courts must compare the value of the property being forfeited with the gravity of the crime.The evidence showed that Smith had purchased the house for $127,967.82 on July 12, 2019. Even without accounting for any appreciation in its value over the following six years, forfeiture would amount to more than 51 times the $2,500 fine imposed on him and more than five times the $25,000 maximum fine authorised for a Class A felony under Arkansas law.The judges also considered the punishment already imposed. Although the offence carried a potential prison sentence of up to 40 years, Smith received supervised probation rather than a lengthy prison term. The court further noted that the drugs and paraphernalia were found inside a removable safe, with no evidence of additional controlled substances, scales or firearms elsewhere in the house. There was also no evidence that Smith himself had been found carrying methamphetamine or that his offence had caused direct harm.Forfeiture order reversed and dismissedThe appeals court concluded that the state's decision to take Smith's entire home went far beyond a proportionate punishment for his offence. It also referred to the Arkansas Constitution, which recognises the right to property as a fundamental protection.Accordingly, the court held that forfeiting the house was grossly disproportionate and violated the Eighth Amendment. It reversed the circuit court's forfeiture order and dismissed the case.The ruling makes clear that even when property has a sufficient connection to a criminal offence to qualify for forfeiture under state law, the government cannot automatically take it. When a forfeiture is punitive, its value must also be proportionate to the seriousness of the offence.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Canadian ski resort that once had chairlifts and hotel buildings is being returned to nature after a $7.5 million fundraising drive; 134 acres will be restored and 885 metres of a public trail protected
articles.summary: A former ski resort in Canada's Beaver Valley, where visitors once used chairlifts and stayed in hotel buildings, is set to become a nature reserve.
articles.body: A former ski resort in Canada's Beaver Valley, where visitors once used chairlifts and stayed in hotel buildings, is set to become a nature reserve. The Bruce Trail Conservancy has raised $7.5 million to remove the resort's old infrastructure, restore its forests and protect wildlife habitats across 134 acres of land.The project will also secure 885 metres of the Bruce Trail, a public hiking route that runs along the Niagara Escarpment in Ontario. The land, near Kimberley in the Municipality of Grey Highlands, will become the Talisman Forest Nature Reserve.The conservancy announced on November 16, 2026, that its Talisman Forever fundraising campaign had reached its $7.5 million target. According to a report by OrilliaMatters, the campaign received more than 1,100 donations from individuals, foundations and other partners. The money will support the permanent protection of the property, removal of the former resort buildings and other infrastructure, ecological restoration and long-term care of the land.From ski resort to nature reserveThe Talisman Mountain Resort once attracted skiers, snowboarders and other visitors to Beaver Valley. It closed in 2011, and its buildings, hotel and restaurant facilities, ski slopes and chairlift infrastructure remained unused for more than a decade.The former resort property became the subject of development proposals, which raised concerns among local residents about the effect on the surrounding natural environment. In 2025, the Bruce Trail Conservancy purchased the portion of the property containing the former ski slopes, resort buildings and land along the Niagara Escarpment. The purchase protected more than 120 acres from future development and secured 885 metres of the Bruce Trail.The conservancy then began planning to restore the 134-acre site and launched the Talisman Forever campaign in April 2026 to raise the money needed for the work. As per the organisation's website, the land will remain protected and publicly accessible as part of Ontario's natural heritage.How the $7.5 million was raisedThe fundraising campaign received support from more than 1,100 donations, along with government contributions. According to OrilliaMatters, Environment and Climate Change Canada provided a $1.5 million matching contribution, while Ontario's Species Conservation Program contributed another $1 million. Both contributions were administered through the Ontario Land Trust Alliance. The remaining support came from private donors, foundations and partners.Forests, grasslands and wildlife habitats to be restoredThe restoration will involve removing the former resort's buildings, chairlifts and other infrastructure, followed by ecological clean-up and reforestation. According to the conservancy's Talisman Forever project website, the former ski slope has created a major gap in the forest cover across a 10-kilometre stretch of Beaver Valley. The plan is to plant native trees and other vegetation to close this gap and provide shade and habitat for wildlife.The organisation is also examining ways to restore meadow and grassland areas. These habitats could support birds such as the eastern meadowlark and bobolink, which have been recorded on the property.The conservancy's ecologists are completing a three-season ecological survey of the land. The survey involves studying the species and natural features found there, and its findings will guide the restoration work.The site includes sugar maple forest, streams, exposed sections of the Niagara Escarpment and slopes that are already beginning to regenerate. The conservancy says the restored landscape will provide habitat for species at risk, pollinators and migratory birds. Its website also identifies benefits such as natural water filtration, flood reduction and carbon storage.Public access to the Bruce Trail will continueThe project is not only about restoring the former resort land. It will also protect a section of the Bruce Trail, one of Canada's best-known hiking routes. The 885-metre section runs along the top of the Niagara Escarpment. Securing it will ensure that the route remains protected and accessible to the public.Ontario Environment Minister Todd McCarthy also welcomed the project. In an October 30 government announcement, he said the province's $1 million contribution would help restore habitat for species at risk while expanding public access to outdoor recreation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Suspects charged in brazen train heist ring that netted $22 million in cargo
articles.summary: More than a dozen people were charged with allegedly orchestrating a massive train heist operation to steal over $22 million in cargo — from popular shoes to power tools — from major retailers.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — More than a dozen people were charged Thursday with allegedly orchestrating a massive train heist operation to steal over $22 million in cargo — from popular shoes to power tools — from major retailers. A federal indictment unsealed on Thursday paints a picture of an organized group that targeted more than three dozen trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear, power tools and other consumer goods that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country. Trains that shuttle goods to stores and customers around the country have become a prominent target for large-scale theft in recent years, especially at large ports in the U.S. that receive hundreds of millions of dollars of shipments every day. The relatively low-tech robberies have demanded attention from the world’s largest retailers, including the likes of Amazon. The men would disable the trains at a planned location by busting the brakes, the indictment alleged, at which point the goods would be offloaded onto trucks. The goods were then peddled to an unnamed company that would resell the stolen merchandise for profit. “The scale of the theft is staggering,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli, promising to prosecute any future efforts to steal the merchandise. In group chats, the men shared numerous photos and videos of themselves busting into the hulking train cars, and posing with wads of cash and stolen merchandise. They also shared AI photos of themselves captioned “Los Trenes,” which means the trains in Spanish, beneath glamorized photos of men throwing boxes of shoes off trains into nearby cars while police helicopters descended overhead. The 13 men were indicted for conspiracy and theft of interstate railroad cargo. Two were also charged with violence against railroad carriers. If convicted, the men could face anywhere from five to 20 years in federal prison.

articles.title: Harambe was killed a decade ago at the same zoo as Fiona
articles.summary: Months of international backlash cast a shadow over the Cincinnati Zoo after workers decided to fatally shoot a beloved endangered gorilla named Harambe in response to a little boy falling into his exhibit in 2016.
articles.body: CINCINNATI — Months of international backlash cast a shadow over the Cincinnati Zoo after workers decided to fatally shoot a beloved endangered gorilla named Harambe in response to a little boy falling into his exhibit in 2016. That outrage faded with the premature birth of an adorable hippo named Fiona, this time bringing worldwide positive attention for the reeling zoo. The zoo shared her miraculous survival in videos and blog posts. They showed her taking a bottle, splashing in a pool and learning to run. She helped restore the zoo’s image. But a decade later, the zoo has found itself in a similarly tragic situation. This time, with Fiona, who died Thursday after eating a visitor’s hat. “Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome,” the zoo said. Widespread mourning quickly started. And nearly as quickly came the comparisons about two beloved animals who captured the world’s attention and whose untimely deaths involved visitors. AI images of the 17-year-old great ape ushering 9-year-old Fiona across the rainbow bridge or the pair surrounded by clouds, next to the gates of heaven were plastered across social media. Some posted that these two deaths show that the zoo needs to do better at keeping animals safe, while others called for compassion for the facility. “As devastated as we are, we cannot begin to fathom the grief that Fiona’s keepers, veterinary team, and the entire Cincinnati Zoo family are experiencing today,” Dino Buddies, a local wildlife outreach company, said in a statement. “We hope that everyone extends these incredible individuals the compassion, kindness, and grace they deserve as they mourn the loss of an animal they loved so deeply.” After Harambe was killed, the zoo reopened its gorilla exhibit with a higher, reinforced barrier. Meanwhile, tongue-in-cheek online petitions sought to add his face to Mount Rushmore or the Lincoln Memorial, and to put him on the dollar bill. There was also a more somber “Justice for Harambe” petition seeking to hold the boy’s mother responsible for his death. The county prosecutor determined there was no cause for charges. In the case of Fiona, Michelle Curley, a zoo spokesperson, said the hat got into her enclosure by accident. It hit a ceiling fan and then got deflected through a small opening above the area’s viewing windows. But that hasn’t quelled the despair. “The two saddest days in all my time here in Cincinnati come from the Zoo,” Marianne King posted on Facebook. The first, she explained, was Harambe’s death and the second was Fiona. Joanne Prater, who lives in the Cincinnati suburb of Loveland, was attending a high school fundraiser Thursday evening and said every person she spoke with talked about how sad they were about Fiona’s death and compared the situation to Harambe. “They are tokens of Cincinnati. You can’t say Fiona or Harambe without everybody knowing who that is here in Cincinnati,” she said. “I guess both of their deaths could have been prevented, but unfortunately accidents do happen.”

articles.title: Russia unleashes retaliatory barrage on Kyiv bridges
articles.summary: The attack follows Putin’s pledge of ‘painful’ response to Ukraine’s attack on symbolic Crimean bridge.
articles.body:
Russia launched a barrage of air attacks on Ukraine, killing eight people, as it targeted Kyiv’s bridges and infrastructure across the country.

The attacks overnight on Thursday into Friday hit vital transport bridges spanning the Dnipro River in the capital and knocked out power generation in several parts of Ukraine, officials said.

The missile and drone swarms came shortly after Russia’s President Vladimir Putin threatened retaliation for Ukraine’s targeting of a symbolic bridge linking his country with the Crimean Peninsula, which Moscow illegally annexed in 2014.

Eight ⁠people – including six in Kyiv – were killed in the overnight attacks, and ⁠28 wounded, ‌Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said in a social media post.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said ballistic missiles had damaged the Podilskyi, Darnitskyi, and Southern bridges, requiring traffic restrictions across the Dnipro.

Buildings, transport and logistics infrastructure were hit in several districts of the city, the Kyiv City Military Administration said in a statement. Citywide electricity disruptions were also reported.

Elsewhere, Ukrainian sources reported that one person was killed as a strike hit a hospital in the Zaporizhia region. Nuclear ⁠power plants across the country were forced to reduce operations, causing outages in Kyiv and 10 regions, First Deputy ‌Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said.

Russia’s Ministry of Defence said on Friday that road and rail bridges in Kyiv used to transport weapons and military equipment to ⁠the battlefield were targeted. It added that its forces hit defence ⁠industry facilities as well as energy and transport infrastructure in several regions of Ukraine.

The large-scale attack came hours after Putin pledged a “painful” response to Ukraine’s partial destruction of the Kerch Bridge earlier this week. The attack severed the key road link across the Kerch Strait.

“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Putin told reporters on Thursday in China, where he attended a summit with the Chinese and United States presidents. Putin said the roadside of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” and pledged to rebuild it.

Ukraine continued its efforts to target energy and military infrastructure overnight. Russia’s Defence Ministry reported that its forces had intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones.

A Ukrainian drone ⁠attack damaged an ⁠industrial facility in Russia’s western ‌region of Smolensk, Governor Vasily Anokhin said on the ⁠Telegram messaging app, ⁠without identifying ⁠the facility.

The commander of Ukraine’s Unmanned ⁠Systems Forces said on Friday that 40 Russian oil ⁠facilities and defence ⁠industry targets have been hit over the past 50 days.

Moscow-installed officials in occupied eastern Ukraine also reported three people had been killed during an attack.

The overnight hostilities illustrate the lack of progress in US-led efforts to mediate a ceasefire.

US envoy Jared Kushner said on Thursday that Russia is comfortable with Europe joining the negotiations, and also with the idea of security guarantees for post-war Ukraine that are modelled on NATO’s Article 5, under which an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all.

Early on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said cooperation between Ukraine, the US and Europe on negotiations is “becoming closer” and that he hoped the US would organise the first multilateral meeting involving the Europeans “as soon as possible”.

Russian ⁠Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said ⁠later that ⁠a visit by three European Union representatives to Russia ‌is “under consideration”.

However, he added that any form of Ukrainian membership of NATO is unacceptable to Moscow.

“[E]ven the notion of a formula for Ukraine’s quasi-membership of NATO, and the search for some sort of – in inverted commas – ‘creative ⁠solution’ in this area, is an option that is ⁠unacceptable to us. We discuss security guarantees first and foremost in terms of ensuring the security of our own country,” Ryabkov was quoted as saying by the Interfax news agency.

“As far as Ukraine is concerned, let ⁠them recognise the irrevocable nature of our demand ⁠that this state must not join NATO. When that happens, I think the issue of security guarantees can be discussed in one way or another,” Ryabkov was quoted as adding.

articles.title: A Windsor, Connecticut player bought a 200X scratch-off ticket at Bloom’s Discount Liquor and won $1 million, but under a new state rule, the winner’s name will stay secret unless they agree to go public
articles.summary: A routine stop at a liquor store in Windsor, Connecticut, turned into a life-changing moment for one lottery player who walked away with a $1 million
articles.body: A routine stop at a liquor store in Windsor, Connecticut, turned into a life-changing moment for one lottery player who walked away with a $1 million scratch-off prize. The winning ticket was purchased at Bloom’s Discount Liquor, but the identity of the lucky player may never become public unless they choose to reveal it. According to the Connecticut Lottery and reporting by the Hartford Courant, the Windsor resident claimed the top prize in the 200X 4th Edition scratch-off game on Monday, November 16. The player had purchased the $20 ticket from the store at 576 Windsor Avenue and opted to receive a one-time cash payment rather than spread the winnings over several years. The $750,000 payment is the game’s gross cash value, before taxes. The winner could instead have received the full $1 million through an annuity paid over 20 years. The odds of winning the top prize were listed as one in 800,000, making it a particularly rare win.Why the winner’s identity will remain privateThe decision not to identify the winner follows a change in Connecticut’s lottery disclosure rules that took effect on October 1, 2025. Under Public Act 25-112, the Connecticut Lottery Corporation must obtain a winner’s prior written consent before publishing their name or address. The requirement also covers the publication of winners’ photographs.Previously, the lottery could publish winners’ names, although individuals could request to have their names removed from its online winners list. The revised law makes consent the starting point instead. The law does not, however, prevent disclosure under Connecticut’s Freedom of Information Act. It specifically preserves that provision, meaning the restriction applies to the lottery’s own publication of winners’ details rather than creating an absolute guarantee of anonymity in every circumstance.The Connecticut Lottery’s official winners list confirms the November 16 claim, identifying Windsor as the winner’s hometown, Bloom’s Discount Liquor as the retailer and 200X 4TH EDITION as the game. The winner’s name has not been published. The game offered three $1 million top prizes. According to the lottery’s prize information updated on November 16, all three had been claimed, with the game reaching its scheduled end date that day.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Mamdani sets plan to close NYC’s notorious Rikers Island jail
articles.summary: New York City’s Rikers Island jail complex would close by 2032 under a plan announced Friday by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose strategy for finally shuttering the notorious facility hinges on substantially reducing the number of people kept behind bars.
articles.body: NEW YORK — New York City’s Rikers Island jail complex would close by 2032 under a plan announced Friday by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose strategy for finally shuttering the notorious facility hinges on substantially reducing the number of people kept behind bars. The city is all but certain to blow past a legal requirement to close Rikers and replace it with four smaller, more modern jails by 2027. For years, Rikers Island has stood as a symbol of dysfunction, with the network of jails so plagued by violence and overcrowding that a federal judge, citing “ abnormal and unacceptable “ conditions, appointed an outside manager to restore order and implement reforms. Mamdani, a Democrat, has been a vocal proponent of closing Rikers, though the longstanding plan to build new jails has met pushback, including from his predecessor, former Mayor Eric Adams, who opposed federal oversight and borough jails. “It is time to finally close Rikers Island,” Mamdani said in a statement. “For decades, New Yorkers have demanded a correctional system that is safe and humane.” The plan hinges on lowering the city’s inmate population from the more than 6,500 people housed at Rikers to around 4,500. The Mamdani administration is proposing a new slate of diversion and supervised release programs, expanding housing and social services to prevent recidivism, along with restoring an online bail payment system and reducing case delays through various measures. “We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers. Working alongside the City Council, Courts and nonprofit partners, we will meet it — for the people in our custody, the staff who serve them, victims of crime, and every New Yorker,” Mamdani said. Instead of housing prisoners at Rikers — an island in the East River near LaGuardia Airport — the city will shift people to jails in the Bronx, Queens, Brooklyn and Manhattan, as well as a handful of medical facilities for people who need healthcare or psychiatric treatment. The city also plans to reduce the number of beds for women, diverting them into community-based programs. The borough jails are expected to open in Brooklyn in 2029; the Bronx and Queens in 2031; and then Manhattan in 2032, according to City Hall. Criminal justice activists have pushed for decades to close Rikers Island, which has housed jail inmates since the 1930s. In 2019, the New York City Council voted to close the jail complex and replace it with newer jails located in the city’s boroughs, with local lawmakers invoking the names of former prisoners who died, including Kalief Browder, who took his own life at age 22 after being held for three years at Rikers. At the time, city officials had also called for shrinking the jail population to accommodate the closure, but ran into opposition from critics who argued doing so would mean more violent criminals on city streets.

articles.title: Popular video game 'GTA VI' drives fears of dangerous copycat stunts for young players, former cop warns
articles.summary: As "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches, an expert links past "GTA" releases to teens citing the game before robberies, subway surfing and police impersonation.
articles.body: The highly anticipated release of "Grand Theft Auto VI," or "GTA VI," is reigniting concerns about the potential dangers of violent video games, with a law enforcement expert warning parents to pay attention to how younger players distinguish virtual crime from real-life consequences. Released on Thursday, "GTA VI" is the sixth installment in game developer Rockstar Games' crime-adventure franchise. Following a male and female duo through high-stakes checkpoints, the game throws players into a world fueled by gunfire, street races and luxury car heists. The game's release brings about renewed fears of the real-world behavior and crime that has followed previous releases. 'GTA VI' PROMOTIONAL BLITZ HITS CHINA, A COUNTRY WHERE THE GAME ISN'T EVEN APPROVED FOR SALE Fox News Digital spoke with former police captain Joshua Schirard, who said previous installments of the franchise have been linked to instances of young people attempting to imitate criminal activity depicted in the games. "This is not unprecedented," Schirard said, pointing to incidents dating back to the release of "Grand Theft Auto IV" back in 2008. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "We actually saw real crime. We saw some teenagers arrested for robberies, for burglaries right after the release, directly citing that they were imitating the things that they were doing in the game." Concerns resurfaced following the release of "Grand Theft Auto V" when young people allegedly attempted dangerous stunts inspired by the game, including subway surfing. INSIDE THE TEEN TAKEOVERS THREATENING TO EXPLODE THIS SUMMER AS CITIES REMAIN ON EDGE: 'VERY WORRIED' In July 2025, four teens were arrested for surfing a subway train in New York City. The NYPD previously told Fox News Digital that there were 200 reported "apprehensions" due to subway surfing incidents from November 2023 through July 2025. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL Schirard also pointed to several young adults who were arrested for impersonating police officers, saying they directly cited the video game as their inspiration. "Once again, directly citing under their own volition that they are imitating things from the game, so obviously these do have an effect on what we see in real life," he said. Still, Schirard cautioned against assuming that children who play violent video games will inevitably engage in criminal behavior. YOUR KID’S GAMING HABIT COULD BE BUILDING A FUTURE CAREER, NEW SURVEY SHOWS He said there is no clear evidence of a widespread increase in crime corresponding with the release of previous installments. "Just because your kid is into these games and likes playing video games doesn't mean that they are going to go and carry out crime," Schirard said. TOO MUCH SCREEN TIME MAY TRIGGER LASTING BRAIN DELAYS, TOP HEALTH OFFICIAL WARNS Instead, he emphasized the importance of parental involvement and making sure children understand the difference between fictional gameplay and real-world actions. "Do they understand that distinction? Do they understand the difference between fiction and real life and the consequences that really come with some of those actions that they're gonna take part in in the game," he asked. CHRIS HANSEN URGES PARENTS TO TEACH CHILDREN ABOUT ONLINE PREDATORS BEFORE ALLOWING INTERNET ACCESS Rather than simply banning conversations about the game, Schirard encourages parents to take an active interest in what their children are playing. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X "It's probably a really fun game. It's a great opportunity to kind of share in your kid's passions. Go in there, play it with them, watch them, ask them how they're doing and what they're doing," he said. "This is a really good conversation to have and a real way to kind of breach into that subject." CREEPY 'CAT IN THE HAT' TREND TARGETS SCHOOLS AS COSTUMED FIGURE ALLEGEDLY CHASES TEEN GIRL He also uses the "GTA" release to remind parents of dangers posed by social media trends, which can encourage children to recreate dangerous stunts for the sake of "going viral." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Schirard said parents should be particularly mindful of viral challenges circulating on platforms such as TikTok.
